issues.body:
The current Keycloak JavaScript adapter returns a token that you have to manually send on the "Authorization" header on every request. To do this, you would typically require remembering that token in a place accessible by JavaScript (e.g. global variables, `sessionStorage`).

Instead, Keycloak could return a `Set-Cookie` header with the token so that the browser would automatically send it in the `Cookie` header in subsequent requests. This would both be more convenient (no manual token propagation needed) and more secure (using HTTP-only cookies would prevent tokens from being accessible by malicious JavaScript, should a cross-site scripting vulnerability occur).

Keycloak already sends a `Set-Cookie` header back with a token. However, it has a `Path=/realms/<realm>/` attribute that prevents the browser from propagating it to other sites, despite being `SameSite=None`. Additionally, the token is different than the one returned by the JavaScript adapter (it uses a different algorithm), which makes it unusable in some (perhaps all) contexts.

In my particular case, I was trying to [configure Eclipse MicroProfile to use cookies](https://download.eclipse.org/microprofile/microprofile-jwt-auth-2.0/microprofile-jwt-auth-spec-2.0.html#_jwt_and_http_headers) (using `mp.jwt.token.header=Cookie` and `mp.jwt.token.cookie=KEYCLOAK_IDENTITY`) when I found the aforementioned Keycloak limitations: the cookie never reached the backend, and when manually changing the cookie's path in the browser so that it does, MicroProfile complained that the token should have been signed with "RS256" instead of "HS256".
issues.title: Allow cookie-based token propagation (single-page application)

issues.body:
This issue is to investigate if we should support GSS-Native in Keycloak for Kerberos integration and possibly add it (if something needs to be changed in the codebase or docs). The reason is, that it *may* be FIPS compliant (to be doublechecked if it really is).

Related conversation between Alexander Bokovoy and myself:

1) Marek: Thanks, the PR is here if you want to take a look: https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/16478 . Still some test failures need to be figured, but you can take a look already...

This is related to FIPS as in the FIPS environment (on RHEL with FIPS enabled), the Kerberos functionality is not available due the SunJGSS security provider is not FIPS compliant yet and hence it is missing in the java.security. So the idea was to encapsulate all the Kerberos related functionality in Keycloak within a "feature", which is enabled by default, but disabled in FIPS environment. Nothing related to Kerberos protocol itself is changed in this PR and the typical environment should not be changed anyhow as long as Kerberos worked already before in such environment. 


2) Alexander's reply:
> Thanks for the details. I looked also at the referenced bugzilla
> https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2051628 and there are few
> problems here.
>
> I think it should be working with a native GSS API
> (-Dsun.security.jgss.native=true) and this is the only one we support in
> RHEL -- we do not support Oracle's own SunJGSS. With native GSS API use
> it would load MIT Kerberos implementation which works with FIPS.
>
> I do not see Keycloak enforcing -Dsun.security.jgss.native=true
> anywhere.
>
> There is another problem, now FIPS specific. If you go by strict
> compliance, even AES128-CTS-HMAC-SHA1-96 and AES256-CTS-HMAC-SHA1-96
> aren't FIPS compliant because they use a non-FIPS KDF. The proper ones
> are encryption types present in RFC8009 but these aren't supported by
> Active Directory. So, in the end, many customers set up RHEL with FIPS
> and allow AES128-CTS-HMAC-SHA1-96 and AES256-CTS-HMAC-SHA1-96. It is not
> Red Hat's issue -- FIPS compliance is purely between those customers and
> their FIPS auditors.
>
> That still would need an appropriate crypto policy setting on the
> system, e.g. 'update-crypto-policies --set FIPS:AD-SUPPORT' on RHEL to
> allow use of AD-compatible encryption types in FIPS mode.

Forgot to add: I have looked at the PR itself and I think it is good
from the perspective of it only relying on ability to instantiate
GSSManager -- if that succeeds, it would use Kerberos. If not, it would
be disabled. If native GSS API would work with Keycloak in FIPS mode,
we'd get it enabled transparently and your PR would ensure it is used in
FIPS mode.

So from my perspective this looks good. 


3) Marek's reply and 4) Alexander's reply :
> Thanks Alexander, this is very useful info!

> So if I understand you correctly, can you confirm if using native GSS API (property -Dsun.security.jgss.native=true) is FIPS compliant on RHEL 8.6 with OpenJDK 17.0.5? Just for the details, my java version is:

I don't think we have any definitive statement about FIPS compliance for
JDK + native GSS API. It needs to be tested and your test results below show
that it works.

What I know for sure is that we do not support Java's own Kerberos
implementation in FIPS mode and overall do not support it on RHEL.
Java's own implementation of Kerberos protocol does not support almost
every new pre-authentication method we provide in RHEL IdM since ~2014,
for example. It also has no support for Active Directory-specific
changes that happened in past several years and is expected to
completely fail down later this year when Microsoft will rollout an
enforcement for new secure KDC behavior to their clients. 

> openjdk version "17.0.5" 2022-10-18 LTS
> OpenJDK Runtime Environment (Red_Hat-17.0.5.0.8-2.el8_6) (build 17.0.5+8-LTS)
> OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM (Red_Hat-17.0.5.0.8-2.el8_6) (build 17.0.5+8-LTS, mixed mode, sharing)


> I can add that when "-Dsun.security.jgss.native=true" is used, the "GSSManager.getInstance().getMechs()" is able to find both KRB5 OID and Spnego OID. But what worries me a bit is the fact that this property does not seem to be officially documented though? At  least in the java sources of "sun.security.jgss.GSSManagerImpl.USE_NATIVE_PROP" I can see comment stating "Undocumented property" .

It is documented for quite some time, for example:
https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/technotes/guides/security/jgss/jgss-features.html
https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/11/security/accessing-native-gss-api.html

Please also look at discussion in https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1026709

> Also I saw some issue when I've tried to test the real SPNEGO workflow. But I guess I need to install and setup some MIT Kerberos packages on my RHEL to be able to proceed?

> Just for the reference (if you have some quick idea, hints or documentation), the exception currently thrown during spnego handshake on Keycloak side:
```
Caused by: GSSException: No valid credentials provided
    at java.security.jgss/sun.security.jgss.wrapper.NativeGSSFactory.getCredFromSubject(NativeGSSFactory.java:59)
    at java.security.jgss/sun.security.jgss.wrapper.NativeGSSFactory.getCredentialElement(NativeGSSFactory.java:112)
    at java.security.jgss/sun.security.jgss.GSSManagerImpl.getCredentialElement(GSSManagerImpl.java:174)
    at java.security.jgss/sun.security.jgss.GSSCredentialImpl.add(GSSCredentialImpl.java:439)
    at java.security.jgss/sun.security.jgss.GSSCredentialImpl.<init>(GSSCredentialImpl.java:89)
    at java.security.jgss/sun.security.jgss.GSSManagerImpl.createCredential(GSSManagerImpl.java:141)
    at org.keycloak.federation.kerberos.impl.SPNEGOAuthenticator.establishContext(SPNEGOAuthenticator.java:165)
    at org.keycloak.federation.kerberos.impl.SPNEGOAuthenticator$AcceptSecContext.run(SPNEGOAuthenticator.java:132)
    at org.keycloak.federation.kerberos.impl.SPNEGOAuthenticator$AcceptSecContext.run(SPNEGOAuthenticator.java:122)
```

I do not see any protocol trouble below. It just that you have no active
Kerberos credentials and your app couldn't use them.

Either:
 - default ccache should contain already valid credentials, or
 - KRB5CCNAME should point to a ccache with valid credentials, or
 - KRB5_CLIENT_KTNAME should point to a keytab that can be used to obtain
   initial credentials with the principal in question

See man kerberos(7) for environmental variables.

You are using 'null' in createCredential() call for the principal, so a
default principal would be used here, e.g. if there is a ticket in a
ccache, or the library would default to a username an app runs under.
However, since your code defines a service credential (ACCEPT_ONLY) use,
then you need to provide a keytab in order to automatically enable TGT
acquisition because otherwise it cannot obtain a ticket at all.
issues.title: Support for native GSSAPI

issues.body:
### Description

This feature proposal is to add an SPI provider specific to Traefik, just like there are specific ones for Apache, HAPROXY, and NGINX.

It would support specificities of the header value produced by the [PassTLSClientCert middleware](https://doc.traefik.io/traefik/middlewares/http/passtlsclientcert/) containing the client certificate.

### Discussion

A related issue on Traefik repository: https://github.com/traefik/traefik/issues/9669

### Motivation

On the Traefik project, we have seen quite a few community use cases involving Keycloak as an Authorization/Authentication server.

And yet, today, there is no SPI provider implementation specific to Traefik available in Keycloak.
For this reason, some of our users were relying on the NGINX SPI provider, which was unintentionally compatible with the header produced by the PassTLSClientCert middleware in Traefik, which contains the client certificate.

Since v2.9.2, the PassTLSClientCert middleware behavior changed and the client certificate PEM bytes are not URL encoded anymore.

Unfortunately, this new behavior makes the NGINX SPI provider unusable with Traefik v2.9.2+, and constitutes a blocker to upgrade for some users of the Traefik community.

After some investigation, it seems that no available SPI provider that can fit with Traefik v2.9.2+ and that can be an alternative to the NGINX one, so a Traefik dedicated SPI provider is very much needed.

### Details

I'm opening this issue to get approval from the Keycloak maintainers to move forward with opening a PR (which is already ready) with the suggested changes.
issues.title: Traefik SPI Provider

- Users who authenticate through a social identity provider are wanted to re-authenticate more often (regardless of remember-me).
- Users with low privileges can remain idle longer than users with high privileges.
- External people have different limits than those of people from the organization.

issues.body:
### Description

We have multiple use cases, where a user is logged in via auth code flow to their normal work environment. For special actions the user needs to elevate rights (think of su with password) by logging in as administrator (without logging out the other session).

Currently even disabling the cookie login will log out the user session, when I do a new login. So as soon as the user logs in as Administrator they are logged out of their normal session.... even if it is with a different client in the same realm.  

The only solution I found is to start the "long running" client session with offline sessions, so that the refresh works after the elevation. Additionally I had to limit the offline session idle time to behave like a normal session... But this is not accepted by some internal customers.

Is there a better way to have multiple user sessions active within one browser? The applications do not run in the browser, they just use the browser for the OIDC login with MFA (so password grant does not work). I have no problem, if the browser is in private mode (or cookies deleted after each login)... but the "normal" end user won't accept that...  

My proposal would be to
-  bind the session at least to the client and not only to realm
-  (better) alternative: enable one browser flow without cookies or session binding. Logout should only happen via the logout endpoint or timeout.
 
I'm open for other proposals or would also write my own login action, if somebody could point to the right starting place...

### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

_No response_

### Details

_No response_

In a cloud installation, there is an explicit separation between global and application resources. A Keycloak deployment is a global resource and, depending on architecture, a realm could be too. However, an application which is supposed to authenticate against that deployment and that realm needs certain resources which are application-specific but need to be configured in the Keycloak instance. ### Description

As of Quarkus 3, persistence configurations in the properties file and a persistence XML file don't work together. 

See: https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/17664#issuecomment-1468620535 and https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/19387#discussion_r1152367232

Quarkus will print a warning on every start: 

> A legacy persistence.xml file is present in the classpath. This file will be used to configure JPA/Hibernate ORM persistence units, and any configuration of the Hibernate ORM extension will be ignored. To ignore persistence.xml files instead, set the configuration property 'quarkus.hibernate-orm.persistence-xml.ignore' to 'true'.

I assume this is "the new way" of Quarkus 3, and we can't use the options any more as long as we continue to use a variant of `persistence.xml`. See also the [migration guide](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/wiki/Migration-Guide-3.0#using-persistence-xml-files-and-quarkus-hibernate-orm-configuration-properties-in-the-same-application-will-fail) for details.

So this task might be to migrate all persistence.xml to properties in the Quarkus world. 

This might also be the way to support multiple persistence units when working with custom user providers ... we need to test if the current example still works.

Let's see if one could get rid of the warning?

issues.body:
### Description

On an IDP details when the Request Refresh Token option is Enabled there should appear an option to Refresh Access Token.
When Refresh Access Token is Enabled and an User logs in through that IDP, while the session is alive, Keycloak should use the requested Refresh Token to refresh the Access Token for that IDP.

### Discussion

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions/15938

### Motivation

Some IDPs only allow using `requested_token_type: urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token`. For example, Google. The problem is that those access_token are short-lived and there's no way to renew them unless your app goes and [retrieves the external IDP tokens](https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_development/index.html#retrieving-external-idp-tokens). But retrieving the external idp tokens defeats the purpose of the token exchange and requires a client with more permissions than what sometimes would be desirable.

Right now there's really no good solution for this use case as far as I understand and I think this would be a possible solution. Even for IDPs that allow for `requested_token_type: urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:refresh_token` it would be a better user experience if there Keycloak could handle the access token refreshing and I would just need to exchange access tokens.

Another solution would be to allow for `requested_token_type: urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:refresh_token` on this types of IDPs (Google, etc.) when the Request Refresh Token is enabled on that IDP.

### Details

I'm not familiar with the code but if manpower is needed I'm open to getting my hands dirty to make this happen. As far as design ideas, it's mostly what I already described.
issues.title: Automatically Refresh IDP Access Token for Token Exchange

issues.body:
### Description

Currently, Keycloak only supports a self-contained token. How about supporting also reference token?

Discussion: https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions/19649

I have already implemented PoC codes for it the by following the specifications and confirmed that they work well as I expected.

### How to manage the cache holding relationship between a self-contained token and a reference token
  - Keycloak does not hold such the cache by itself. A user of Keycloak who wants to use a reference token needs to prepare the cache. Keycloak only defines I/F with the cache.

### Target tokens
  - an access token and a refresh token returned from Token endpoint (excluding an access token returned in an authorization response by OIDC Hybrid flow).

### Keycloak -> a client - converting a self-contained token to a reference token:
  1. Generating and returning an access/refresh token:
   - Endpoint: Token endpoint
   - Protocol flow: Authorization code flow, Device authorization flow, OIDC Backchannel authentication flow (CIBA)
  2. Re-generating and returning an access/refresh token:
   - Endpoint: Token endpoint
   - Protocol flow: Token refresh

###  A client/resource server -> Keycloak - converting a reference token to a self-contained token:
  1. Receiving a token refresh request:
   - Endpoint: Token endpoint
   - Token: a refresh token
   - Protocol flow: Token refresh
  2. Receiving a token introspect request:
   - Endpoint: Token Introspection endpoint
   - Token: an access token, a refresh token
   - Protocol flow: Token introspection
  3. Receiving a UserInfo request:
   - Endpoint: UserInfo endpoint
   - Token: an access token
   - Protocol flow: UserInfo request
  4. Receiving a token revoke request:
   - Endpoint: Token revocation endpoint
   - Token: an access token, a refresh token
   - Protocol flow: Token revoke request
  5. Receiving a backchannel logout (legacy) request:
   - Endpoint: Logout endpoint
   - Token: a refresh token
   - Protocol flow: Backchannel logout (legacy, not OIDC for logout compliant)

 ### How to convert a self-contained token to a reference token and vise versa:
  - Abstract class of client policies' executor (SPI provider)

 ### How to generate a reference token
  - Concrete class of client policies' executor (SPI provider), so a user of Keycloak can customize it.

 ### How to define and implement I/F an external cache holding relationship between a self-contained token and a reference token:
  - Concrete class of client policies' executor (SPI provider), so a user of Keycloak can customize it.

### Actual reference implementation of such the I/F with the cache:
  - I/F: REST API
    - bind and store the relationship between a self-contained token and a reference token
      - Request (application/json): a reference token, a self-contained token
      - Method: POST
      - Response
        - 204 No Content
        - 400 Bad Request
        - 500 Internal Server Error
    - get the self-contained token bound with the reference token
      - Request: the reference token
      - Method: GET
      - Response (application/json)
        - 200 OK: the self-contained token
        - 400 Bad Request
        - 500 Internal Server Error

### Actual reference implementation of a reference token
 - Format: "jti" claim value of a self-contained token

### Discussion

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions/19649

### Motivation

  - Privacy: Some use cases require not including sensitive data like Personal Identifiable Information (PII) in an access token.
  - Confidentiality: Not disclosing information which a resource server only need to know to 3rd party entities like clients.
  - Security requirement: Some use cases requires a reference token as their requirement.

### Details

 - Cache: Keycloak does not implement such the cache by itself. Instead of it, Keycloak defines I/F with the cache and a user of Keycloak prepares it implementing the I/F, which burdens a user of Keycloak who want to use a reference token. However, Keycloak itself and other user who uses a self-contained token as usual are not affected by supporting a reference token.
 - Non-invasive way: a reference token is realized by client policies, which means that Keycloak's body codes and other user who uses a self-contained token as usual are not affected by supporting a reference token.
 - Flexibility: by using client policies, it is easy to specify which clients use a reference token. Namely, we can select using a reference token or a self-contained token per client.
 - Flexibility: a user of Keycloak can implement their own I/F with the cache as a SPI provider.
issues.title: Supporting reference access/refresh tokens

issues.body:
### Before reporting an issue

- [X] I have searched existing issues
- [X] I have reproduced the issue with the latest release

### Area

dist/quarkus

### Describe the bug

I am using the Keycloak Quarkus docker image. As per the documentation (https://www.keycloak.org/server/configuration#_setup_of_the_initial_admin_user), if you set KEYCLOAK_ADMIN and KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD environment variables it will create the administrative user if they do not already exist.

This part works as expected.

The problem is that I am trying to recover from accidental deletion of  the administrative user. Upon restart of the container, the KEYCLOAK_ADMIN user _should_ be recreated.

However, there is a quirk in the code which is preventing this from happening _when_ there are other users which have been created in the master realm.

The appliance bootstrap runs the createMasterRealmUser() function https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/main/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/managers/ApplianceBootstrap.java#L99 when attempting to recreate the KEYCLOAK_ADMIN user.

it has the following lines in it

```java
        if (session.users().getUsersCount(realm) > 0) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Can't create initial user as users already exists");
        }
```
However, when the Quarkus runtime receives this exception here https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/main/quarkus/runtime/src/main/java/org/keycloak/quarkus/runtime/KeycloakMain.java#L161 it calls the ServicesLogger.LOGGER.addUserFailedUserExists which misreports that it can't add the KEYCLOAK_ADMIN user again. 

Here is the returned error log (my KEYCLOAK_ADMIN user was called 'administrator')

```
2023-04-23 15:33:53,141 ERROR [org.keycloak.services] (main) KC-SERVICES0010: Failed to add user 'administrator' to realm 'master': user with username exists
```

So you see that the error message is misleading. The user does not exist, the problem is the session.users().getUsersCount(realm) > 0 check which will not create the user if there are _any_ other users on the realm. 

I think this check should be replaced with code which checks whether the named user exists already, rather than the presence of any other users.

### Version

21

### Expected behavior

I would expect the KEYCLOAK_ADMIN user to be recreated, even if other users have been recreated on the master realm in the meantime.



### Actual behavior

The KEYCLOAK_ADMIN user is not recreated as it is not allowing it to be created if any users exist in the master realm.

The error message given in the logs is incorrect.

### How to Reproduce?

1. Install Keycloak from docker image setting KEYCLOAK_ADMIN and KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD
2. Create another user on the master realm
3. Delete the KEYCLOAK_ADMIN user
4. Restart the container
5. Observe that the KEYCLOAK_ADMIN user is not recreated

### Anything else?

I think this is quite important to fix, given that this process may be needed to rescue an installation where the administrative user has been accidentally deleted.
issues.title: Support for admin recovery

### Before reporting an issue

- [X] I have searched existing issues
- [X] I have reproduced the issue with the latest release

### Area

oidc

### Describe the bug

Keycloak contains a hard-coded rule that will not let the "iss" claim be set to a custom value in an "access token". 

### Version

20.0.5

### Expected behavior

This can  be demonstrated by adding a hard-coded claim to a client scope, when you attempt to fetch an access token for that client an error will be written to the log file. If we had a Keycloak instance configured with such a client we might issue the following request:

```shell
curl https://my-keycloak-instance/auth/realms/myrealm/protocol/openid-connect/token \
  -H 'Cache-Control: nocache' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -d 'grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=CLIENT_ID&client_secret=SECRET_GOES_HERE'
```

I would expect the "iss" value in the token to be the values specified in the hard-coded claim.


### Actual behavior

Instead the following message would appears in the log file...

> Claim "iss" is non-modifiable in IDToken. Ignoring the assignment for mapper 'hardcoded-iss-mapper'.

...And the returned JWT token would have the URL for the Keycloak instance in the "iss" claim.

### How to Reproduce?

Add a hard-coded claim to a client scope that sets the "iss" value, then request an access token.

### Anything else?

While having the URL for Keycloak in the "iss" claim makes a lot of sense for a variety of use-cases, I would argue that it is not the right thing to do for _every_ use case. It is a reasonable default but we need to enable people to provide their own value when that is what makes sense for their situation.

In my own experience, I need to perform backend authentication to a third party service. This third party has a clear list of what they need to see in the claims of the token, including a specific value in the "iss" claim. While I don't like this requirement I am powerless to change the mind of this third party (who looms large in the hospital-wide electronic health record space).

By way of filling in some history on this issue, it was originally change in https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/8680, this PR was addressing issue 14309.

https://issues.redhat.com/browse/KEYCLOAK-14309?attachmentViewMode=list

I have patched my Keycloak instance in order to verify that this was the root cause, the patch is very short. I removed line 111 from the `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/mappers/OIDCAttributeMapperHelper.java` file.

I realize that this may not be the best way to resolve this issue. I would be glad to work on this further and submit a PR, please let me know how I should best proceed.

Thank you for your time! 🙂
issues.title: Backend OAuth2 Flow Broken, the "iss" Claim is Hard-Coded to the Keycloak URL

issues.body:
The Operator currently creates `passthrough` Routes by default (if TLS is not configured, unlike Nginx Ingress that uses uses a reencrypt strategy. Passthrough has (among others) performance implications on Keycloak.

We should either make `reencrypt` the default strategy, or make it configurable (affecting both Routes and Nginx Ingress).

**Considerations**
* This is potentially a breaking change.
* `reencrypt` requires configuring the Route to trust the Keycloak's certificate. This might be a bit tricky doing manually and not something we want to force the users to do. Keycloak should be automatically configured to use TLS key/cert that is generated by OpenShift CA (and therefore implicitly trusted by the Routes).

**Workaround**
Disable the default Ingress and create a custom Route.
issues.title: Add support for `reencrypt` OpenShift Routes to the Operator

issues.body:
### Description

A user should be given a unique persistent id that is still available after an export/import. Currently, Keycloak creates a new user id.



### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

A major advantage of Keycloak is the vendor-independent use of an IAM. However, this advantage can hardly be exploited due to the missing feature. 

Why is this feature so important for us?
During development we work with a local Keycloak instance. As soon as the product grows, we will move the Keycloak instance to a dev cloud. We are already working with the first friendly users. Eventually, keycloak will be moved to a fully managed service. with each keycloak move, all our clients have to be fixed. Especially with the fully managed services, there is a problem because we don't have access to the keycloak database.

The only uniq property that Keycloak currently provides after an export and import is the user name. User names are editable depending on the configuration. This means that as soon as a user changes his user name, all dependent keycloak clients must know about the change. Otherwise, the user loses all his references in the clients. This is the reason why I prefer to use the user id in all clients. But this is lost after an export / import.

The problem can be partially compensated for by custom user attributes. However, this requires an additional custom service that makes this possible. Ultimately, this leads to a messy ping pong registry flow with messy workarounds.



### Details

Since Keycloak uses a uuid for the user id, this can be retained during an export and import. 

Alternatively, another native user property can be implemented "external user id". This is NOT used for internal keycloak referencing. This property value is still availible after import. This property must be provided by Keycloak uniq.  This property must be provided by Keycloak in the access token.
issues.title: Uniq persistent user ID for external use

issues.body:
### Description

Caddy is a relatively new web server. To support Caddy as a reverse proxy provider for client certificate authentication, the Keycloak team will need to add support for Base64-encoded DER certificates. As of right now, Keycloak only supports PEM files.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

While Caddy is a new web server, it is not uncommon. Caddy has been used by Cloudflare in their implementation of their MITM protection service; separately, Let's Encrypt considers Caddy's "implementation of [ACME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automatic_Certificate_Management_Environment) to be the gold standard of ACME clients," per [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caddy_(web_server)). Supporting Caddy would be a great addition to Keycloak as more enterprises consider Caddy for their web server needs.

### Details

Per the [lead developer](https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/issues/3767#issuecomment-1574294070), Caddy will not support passing PEM-formatted certificates in HTTP headers, and instead only supports B64-encoded DERs; therefore, the standard Apache, Nginx and HAProxy provider options do not work with Caddy. Caddy also does not automatically construct a certificate chain when passing a client certificate, similar to how Nginx currently works (Keycloak documentation mentions this [here](https://www.keycloak.org/server/reverseproxy) under "Configuring the NGINX provider").

My ask is to add Caddy as a reverse proxy provider. This would be nearly identical to the Nginx provider, except Keycloak must accept B64'ed DER certificates. As of right now, if a DER certificate is passed to Keycloak via Caddy, the following error occurs, as the format lacks the expected new line characters:

```
ERROR [org.keycloak.services] (executor-thread-50) org.keycloak.common.util.PemException: org.bouncycastle.jcajce.provider.asymmetric.x509.CertificateFactory$ExCertificateException: parsing issue: 
long form definite-length more than 31 bits: java.security.GeneralSecurityException: org.keycloak.common.util.PemException: org.bouncycastle.jcajce.provider.asymmetric.x509.CertificateFactory$ExCertificateException: parsing issue: long fo
rm definite-length more than 31 bits
```
issues.title: Support Caddy as a Reverse Proxy Provider for Client Certificate Authentication

### Description

Please include the `quarkus-config-yaml` Quarkus extension (https://quarkus.io/guides/config-yaml) in Keycloak.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

The YAML format has many advantages over the Java properties format, to name a few:
* it is easier to work with - think tools like [helm](https://helm.sh/), which support it natively
* terser, more readable - cf.
  ```properties
  quarkus.datasource.extrads.jdbc.url=jdbc:oracle:thin:@//hostname:1521/DBNAME
  quarkus.datasource.extrads.jdbc.new-connection-sql=ALTER SESSION SET CURRENT_SCHEMA = "APP-SCHEMA"
  quarkus.datasource.extrads.jdbc.acquisition-timeout=PT30S
  quarkus.datasource.extrads.username=scott
  quarkus.datasource.extrads.password=tiger
  ```
  with:
  ```yaml
  quarkus:
    datasource:
      extrads:
        jdbc:
          url: jdbc:oracle:thin:@//hostname:1521/DBNAME
          new-connection-sql: |-
            ALTER SESSION SET CURRENT_SCHEMA = "APP-SCHEMA"
          acquisition-timeout: PT30S

        username: scott
        password: tiger
  ```
* less error prone

### Details

The extension can actually be added even to the current Keycloak releases just by putting the following two jar files (all other dependencies are already included):
- [quarkus-config-yaml-2.13.7.Final.jar](https://mvnrepository.com/artifact/io.quarkus/quarkus-config-yaml/2.13.7.Final)
- [smallrye-config-source-yaml-2.12.3.jar](https://mvnrepository.com/artifact/io.smallrye.config/smallrye-config-source-yaml/2.12.3)

to the `/opt/keycloak/providers` directory of the official docker image and running `/opt/keycloak/bin/kc.sh build`.
Together those two jar files are less than 20kB in size, which is IMO negligible.

issues.body:
### Description

The [OpenID Connect RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 spec](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-rpinitiated-1_0.html#RPLogout) suggests that a `logout_hint` parameter can be used instead of the `id_token_hint`.

We would like to contribute support for _logout_hint_ for the OIDC Identity Provider.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

Sometimes the ID token of an Identity Provider contains so much data, that the logout url - containing the ID Token as `id_token_hint` parameter - becomes too large to be handled by some browsers/servers.

We have faced this issue with Azure AD, where some of our customers have lots of roles or groups defined. Limiting the token by filtering the roles/groups is not an option for some of the customers, because most of them are relevant for their applications.

To circumvent logout failures, we have implemented a custom OIDC Identity Provider which supports the `logout_hint` feature supported by Azure AD.

### Details

It is not specified in the spec, which value this `logout_hint` should contain. Azure AD requires a special claim named `login_hint` (not to be confused with the parameter of the same name, which can be used for OIDC login), see https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory/develop/v2-protocols-oidc#send-a-sign-out-request.

Probably it makes sense to support a flexible configuration for the OIDC Identity Provider implementation. It could be configurable whether `id_token_hint` or `logout_hint` should be used for logout. When `logout_hint` is selected, the key of an ID token claim could be specified, which provides the value to be used for logout. For Azure AD, this would be `login_hint`.  For Auth0, it would be `sid` (see https://auth0.com/docs/authenticate/login/logout/log-users-out-of-auth0).

WDYT of  supporting the `logout_hint` parameter?
issues.title: OIDC Identity Provider: Support logout_hint as an alternative to id_token_hint for OIDC logout

### Description

I want to use Keycloak on OpenShift (OCP) and want to make sure there is `Route` created for Keycloak, even if I had not specified upfront the hostname value for Keycloak to use.

Seems that Keycloak operator assumes that `Route` for Keycloak is auto-generated by OpenShift based on the `Ingress` resource creates, granted one specifies `className: openshift-default` in the `Keycloak` CR. And then, when if there is `Keycloak.spec.hostname` specified, [adds](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/main/operator/src/main/java/org/keycloak/operator/controllers/KeycloakIngress.java#L111) the `host` into `Ingress` resource created.


However, on OCP 4.12+, [`route-controller-manager`](https://github.com/openshift/route-controller-manager) creates `Route` based on the `Ingress` resource, [ONLY if the `Ingress` resource has `.spec.rules.host` specified](https://github.com/openshift/route-controller-manager/blob/main/pkg/route/ingress/ingress.go#L416), otherwise no `Route` is created.

It is perfectly valid to create `Route` on OpenShift, without `host` being specified - in such case, OCP auto-generated the host in the `*.apps.<cluster-dns-name>` subdomain.

So, my key questions are:
- Is the assumption that `hostname` is specified in `Keycloak` CR correct - i.e. is this parameter absolutely required for Keycloak application to work correctly?
  - what breaks when `hostname` is not specified in `Keycloak` CR?
- If `hostname` parameter is not required, should we have the updated Keycloak operator logic in the appropriate way, so that `Route` is created on OpenShift (perhaps a strict tie to Ingres->Route autogeneration could be revised?)

A bit related discussion: https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/20128 , since eventually we'd like to use the re-encrypt Routes, with the certifies being rotated and replaced with customer's certificates.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

Using Keyclok on OpenShift requires `Route` to be exposed outside of the cluster, for external applications / processes interactions.

### Details

_No response_

issues.body:
### Description

The actual mechanism for importing CSS, JS and favicon in the `theme.property` config file is very limited.

#### Documentation

According to the doc, to import JS or CSS, it is like this:
```ini
styles=file1.css file2.css ...
scripts=file1.js file2.js ...
favicon=favicon.ico
```

#### Problems

A problem with CSS imports: it is not possible to conditionally import them using media query. An example is with the dark/light theme:
```html
<link href=${url.resourcesPath}/css/light.css" media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" rel="stylesheet" type="text/css"/>
<link href=${url.resourcesPath}/css/dark.css" media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" rel="stylesheet" type="text/css"/>
```

A problem with favicon: it is not possible to use variants. An example is with compatibility:
```html
<link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="${url.resourcesPath}/favicon/favicon.svg" />
<link rel="icon" type="image/png" href="${url.resourcesPath}/favicon/favicon.png" />
<link rel="icon" type="image/x-icon" href="${url.resourcesPath}/favicon/favicon.ico" />
```

And an example with favicon variants and dark/ligth theme:
```html
<link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="${url.resourcesPath}/favicon/favicon.svg" />
<link rel="icon" type="image/png" href="${url.resourcesPath}/favicon/favicon-light.png" media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" />
<link rel="icon" type="image/png" href="${url.resourcesPath}/favicon/favicon-dark.png" media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" />
```

I'm sure we can find other examples.

One last issue: mixing `theme.property` imports and html `<link|script />` imports is not consistent.
And should probably be avoided.


#### New Features

The motivation for this release is to add a more advanced way to import JS/CSS/favicon:
* Supports CSS media queries
* Supports favicon variants
* Supports favicon types (automatic or manual)
* Supports integrity checksum
* Supports defer property



### Discussion

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions/21999

### Motivation

There are three reasons:
* The official documentation does not support either the `<link|script />` method; so, compliance with future releases is not guaranteed, and therefore it's not a recommended method.
* Mixing `theme.property` imports and html `<link|script />` imports is inconsistent and a source of bugs.
* This would ensure that the Keycloak template code is as close as possible to alongside web applications.

### Details

I think an easy way to add this feature without breaking the actual code is to add extra parameters that stick to the filename.

For example:
```ini
styles=file1.css file2-light.css[media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)"] file2-dark.css[media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"] ...
scripts=file1.js file2.js[integrity="hexahash", defer="defer"] ...
favicons=favicon.svg favicon-light.png[media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)"] favicon-dark.png[media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"] favicon.ico
```

Because of the Java properties file, perhaps a better solution is to also support a JSON file. So, the developer can choose between these two formats.

For example:
```json5
{
	"styles": [
		"file1.css",
		{ "name":"file2-light.css", "media":"(prefers-color-scheme: light)" }
		{ "name":"file2-dark.css", "media":"(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" }
		// ...
	],
	"scripts": [
		"file1.js",
		{ "name":"file2.js", "integrity":"hexahash", "defer":"defer" }
		// ...
	],
	"favicons": [
		"favicon.svg",
		{ "name":"favicon-light.png", "media":"(prefers-color-scheme: light)" },
		{ "name":"favicon-dark.png", "media":"(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" },
		"favicon.ico"
		// ...
	]
}
```
issues.title: More flexible imports in custom theme (i.e. CSS media queries)

### Description

Currently, it is possible to enable multiple languages for Keycloak themes by the internationalization setting in the realm Settings of Keycloak. 
However, there is no option to tell Keycloak to simply use the browser language and hide the Language Selector. 

It would be nice to simply enable languages and let the browser handle the language selection. 

Due to this missing feature, a custom theme with a custom js script that reloads the page is necessary: 
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/76911328/how-to-force-keycloak-to-use-the-browsers-default-language




### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

Most websites today simply use the browser's default language to choose which texts need to be displayed. 
This is not to say that Language Selectors are completely obsolete or never have a use case, but that the most common way to select the correct language for a UI is the Browser default. 

To achieve this behaviour today the solution is somewhat cumbersome since you have to manually create a script and adapt themes. 

### Details

Well, currently the workaround is this: 
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/76911328/how-to-force-keycloak-to-use-the-browsers-default-language

In the admin console, I would simply propose the option "use Browsers default Language". 
I personally would prefer to enable it by default but I understand if others would have a different preference. 
In addition to that the option "hide Language Selector" would be cool, but it's easier to find and remove in the template.ftl. 
Alternatively the Option "use Browsers default Language" could also hide the Language Selector as well, but that could probably annoy other clients that want the browsers' default but also give the user the option to select another language.

issues.body:
### Description

Sometimes email is as important as password (or not that far)
In our company, we would like to avoid having somes users email available in the DB (or in the admin UI)
So a simple thing could be to simply not consider this email and never assign an email to those users

The problem comes when we want to activate the feature "Reset password"
We found nothing to face this requirement in Keycloak (currently)

However we are interested in contributing to Keyclaok source code to give the following feature : never save clear user email but give the ability to reset the password using email

### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

The main motivation is GDPR/PII regulations

### Details

Here the idea to implement this feature : 
- Save in the DB a transformation of the email `f(email)` where `f` is encryption function (it will depend on random string `s`, we will derivate that email n times to get `d(email)` and use an `HMAC(s, d(email))` to calculate a kind of Hash of that string s. Its to make a little more complex the brute force attack)
- When the user ask to reset his password but dosent have clear email, but has a `f(email)` then we will ask the user to enter his email in a form, then we check that `f(email_in_form)` is equal to our saved `f(email)` in the DB (then we send the reset password email)
- We have to add an input to enter `f(email)` for users in the admin UI (in case the admin want to set it manually). We will not ask the admin to calculate `f(email)`, he will enter only the email but we will transform that without retaining the value before saving into the DB
- For user registration, a button should be added to ask the user if he wants to save his email in clear way or not. (This point is not needed for our company, but should be considered if we want to deliver a complete and logic feature)
- Since its adding complexity to the use of Keycloak, this feature can be hidden by default and maybe we can enable it with flag like `--features="...,secret_email"`

We are aware that a brute force attack can break our protection system but we found nothing better for the moment.

**Any suggestion or opinion is welcome.**
issues.title: Never save clear user email

issues.body:
### Description

1. It would be a security benefit if certain realms could have different i.e., more restricted values for the maximum size, and maximum number of additional parameters for an authentication request.
2. Also, the strategy to silently ignore additional request parameters that do not meet the requirements (number, length) is not suitable for everyone, as it does not enforce the fail-fast behavior.
3. Additional configuration support is also enabled by using a maximum size for all additional request parameter length combined.

1. The current values for `ADDITIONAL_REQ_PARAMS_MAX_MUMBER` is `5` and for `ADDITIONAL_REQ_PARAMS_MAX_SIZE` is `2000` (see https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/c0c0a80/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/endpoints/request/AuthzEndpointRequestParser.java#L41).
2. The default behavior is still to silently ignore the additional request parameters. If the toggle is switched, an exception will be raised.
3. The default value is `Integer.MAX_VALUE`.

Configurable value enables customers to harden their keycloak instances realm specific by reducing the values according to their needs. All changes are backwards compatible and do NOT need any special configuration when updating keycloak the this version.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

This feature would enable customers to optionally configure the maximum number of additional parameters, the maximum size of each parameter, whether fail-fast strategy should be used and whether an overall parameter limit should be enforced, without having the need to change the keycloak-core.

### Details

The idea was to be definitely backwards compatible and don't force any configuration when upgrading to a new keycloak version.
issues.title: Use optional realm attribute for authenticationrequest parameter max size/number validation configuration

### Describe the bug

This is related to #10250.

Including a brokered IdP authentication in a flow interferes with step up authentication. 

When IdP authentication happens, it looks like the level of authentication (LOA) is never set on the authentication session. 
When doing IdP authentication, I can see the following TRACE in the log:

> TRACE [org.keycloak.authentication.authenticators.conditional.ConditionalLoaAuthenticator] (default task-1) Condition 'Level 1' evaluated to true due the user not yet reached any authentication level in this session, configuredLoa: 1, requestedLoa: 1

When the flow does not include IdP authentication, I see the following:

> TRACE [org.keycloak.authentication.authenticators.conditional.ConditionalLoaAuthenticator] (default task-2) Updating LoA to '1' in the condition 'Level 1' when authenticating session 'a8f51bd7-8593-4733-b731-8a863e2e4d8d'. Max age is 36000.
>
>  TRACE [org.keycloak.authentication.authenticators.conditional.ConditionalLoaAuthenticator] (default task-2) Condition 'Level 2' evaluated to false due the requestedLoa '1' smaller than configuredLoa '2'. CurrentAuthenticationLoa: 1
>
>  TRACE [org.keycloak.authentication.authenticators.conditional.ConditionalLoaAuthenticator] (default task-2) Finished authentication at level 1 when authenticating authSession 'a8f51bd7-8593-4733-b731-8a863e2e4d8d'.
>
>  TRACE [org.keycloak.authentication.authenticators.conditional.ConditionalLoaAuthenticator] (default task-2) Updating authenticated levels in authSession 'a8f51bd7-8593-4733-b731-8a863e2e4d8d' to user session note for future authentications: {"1":1701809618}
> 

Since the LOA is not set in the authentication session, refreshing the page causes the login prompt to be displayed even though the user has an active session. This is because the CookieAuthenticator contains some logic that checks the LOA and fails if it's not the correct level:
```

    if (acrStore.getRequestedLevelOfAuthentication() > previouslyAuthenticatedLevel) {
        // Step-up authentication, we keep the loa from the existing user session.
        // The cookie alone is not enough and other authentications must follow.
        acrStore.setLevelAuthenticatedToCurrentRequest(previouslyAuthenticatedLevel);
        context.attempted();
```


### Version

Any

### Expected behavior

LOA should be set in the authentication session

### Actual behavior

See above

### How to Reproduce?

Define a flow including step-up authentication. One of the "branches" in the flow should include authentication against an external IdP.

issues.body:
### Description

With with Keycloak LDAP sync feature, when a user is removed from LDAP they are deleted from the Keycloak repository and all users role and profile information is lost.  While in the sunny day scenario this is the correct behavior (e.g. a user has left the company), in the rainy day scenario the user profile must be reconstructed.  There are a number of business reasons why a user's LDAP user could be temporarily removed from the LDAP server. Today when the user is added back into the LDAP they are created as a fresh user in keycloak and the user's roles and permissions will need to be reconstructed from scratch.  There are also other bug tickets in github complaining about communication issues with an LDAP server resulting in users getting deleted from keycloak.  A "recycle bin" option where users deleted from an LDAP sync are put in a "recycle bin" would solve this problem.  Having a distinct recycle bin would ensure that Keycloak admins do not confuse a disabled user with a deleted user put in the recycle bin.  Users deleted from keycloak as a result of an LDAP sync operation could have their userID put into the recycle bin for some configurable period of time (e.g.1 week, 1 month).  And if the user is restored in LDAP keycloak could do a check to see if it should create a new user or restore a user from the recycle bin.  

See issue complaining on keycloak users disappearing because of LDAP sync issues
https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/24669

### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

See above description for explanation on the motivation

### Details

_No response_
issues.title: Recycle bin for keycloak users

issues.body:
### Description

Introduce a new SPI for CORS and create a default implementation based on `org.keycloak.services.resources.Cors`.

### Discussion

_(discussed at 6th OAuth SIG)_

### Motivation

Currently, we have `Cors` class that belongs to `services` and is not visible from other modules. The behavior is mostly hardcoded with limited configurability. The introduction of CORS SPI will help solve the following issues:
* Expose the `Cors` class to the provider infrastructure. Currently, one can only pass `Cors` to a provider as `java.lang.Object` and then cast it back in the implementation ([1](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/main/server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenExchangeContext.java#L43), [2](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/main/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/DefaultTokenExchangeProvider.java#L120)). This will also be required by the upcoming OAuth 2.0 Grant SPI;
* The default implementation will have its configuration namespace (`kc.spi-cors-default`) which will allow to customize the behavior (example: #12682)
* The SPI will allow to replace the built-in CORS implementation with a custom one if needed.

### Details

As long as CORS implementation is going to be a provider, using it will require a `KeycloakSession`. At the OAuth SIG, we have agreed that we can have a new session-based API whilst (temporarily) keeping the old one:
```java
// old API
Cors cors = Cors.add(request);
Cors cors = Cors.add(request, response);

// new API
Cors cors = session.getProvider(Cors.class); // request object will be obtained from KeycloakContext, should cover the absolute majority of cases
Cors cors = session.getProvider(Cors.class).request(request); // override request object
Cors cors = session.getProvider(Cors.class).builder(builder); // set builder
Cors cors = session.getProvider(Cors.class).request(request).builder(builder); // override both, should be rare
```

This will result in the following changes/decisions:
* The `org.keycloak.common.util.Resteasy` class will need to be moved to the `common` module, otherwise it won't be accessible from the `Cors::add` methods (which will need to resolve `KeycloakSession` via a Resteasy context).
issues.title: CORS SPI

### Description

The JGroups communication is not secure between Keycloak servers. JGroups support SSL sockets (http://jgroups.org/manual5/index.html#TLS) but it requires a customized Infinispan XML configuration file.

The work to be done under this issue is to add options to configure the required attributes (basically the keystore and the truststore) and, programmatically, inject the SSL sockets factories in JGroups independently from the Infinispan XML. This way, it works with the default configuration, customs ones, and with the Keycloak Operator in OpenShift.

issues.body:
### Description

Since `MapStorageSpi` and `MAP_STORAGE`-feature have been removed, it became quite challenging to replace Keycloak storage including Infinispan-caching with a custom implementation. I understand that supporting something like map store was too big in scope and very challenging for the core team. Thus i am proposing a kind of middle ground: A CustomDatastore-feature which disables all of the default storage providers to simplify replacing them with custom implementations.

If you support this idea, i could provide the implementation.

### Discussion

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions/24052

### Motivation

Right now, to replace default datastore one not only has to implement `DatastoreProvider` but also needs to make sure that default implementations are not loaded (as they register themselves as event listeners, start infinispan-caches, do JPA-database migrations, etc inside of `init()`).
This was taken care of in KC < 23 when `Feature.MAP_STORAGE` was enabled, as all "Legacy"-providers where then disabled via `EnvironmentDependentProviderFactory.isSupported()`.

This is no longer the case in KC 23. Thus to achieve the same we did not find another way than either disabling all the default providers (cumbersome) or overriding them by using the same ID and a higher `order()` (weird).
And currently there is no way at all to disable JPA/Cache Quarkus-BuildSteps.

### Details

- Add a `CUSTOM_DATASTORE`-feature (experimental)
- If this feature is activated, all default storage providers are deactivated via `EnvironmentDependentProviderFactory` (basically replace all occurences of `!Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.MAP_STORAGE)` from KC < 23 with `!Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.CUSTOM_DATASTORE)`
- Introduce `IsCustomDatastoreEnabled` BooleanSupplier (based on `IsLegacyStoreEnabled` from KC < 23) to disable Cache- and JPA-Quarkus-BuildSteps

### Description

In order to issue Verifiabel Credentials to Wallets, Keycloak should support the [OpenID for Verifiable Credentials Issuance(OID4VCI) Protocol](https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-credential-issuance-1_0.html). The protocol is intended to offer and issue credentials to wallets in a secure and standard way. 


### Discussion

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions?discussions_q=is%3Aopen+label%3Aarea%2Foid4vc

### Motivation

OID4VCI seems to be the most mature and used issuance protocol at the moment. Its already used and mandated by various projects:

* [EUDI Wallet Architecture](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/european-digital-identity-wallet-architecture-and-reference-framework)
* [EBSI](https://ec.europa.eu/digital-building-blocks/sites/display/EBSI)

* [DSBA Technical Convergence](https://data-spaces-business-alliance.eu/wp-content/uploads/dlm_uploads/Data-Spaces-Business-Alliance-Technical-Convergence-V2.pdf)

Implementing wallets can for example be found at the [EBSI conformant wallets](https://ec.europa.eu/digital-building-blocks/sites/display/EBSI/Conformant+wallets).

https://github.com/francis-pouatcha/keycloak-community/blob/OIDC4VCI-Design-2/design/OID4VCI.md

### Discussion

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/20677

### Motivation

There are two cases when updating the broker link when duplicates exists.
case 1:
```
[before]
User A:
 - username: user_a
 - broker_user: 
     - username: user_a
     - user_id: id_1

when the new broker_link comes
(This happens when the broker_user create a new account but use the previous username)
broker_user:
    - username: user_a
    - user_id: id_2

[after]
User A:
 - username: user_a
 - broker_user: 
     - username: user_a
     - user_id: id_2
 ```

case 2:
```
[before]
User A:
 - username: user_a
 - broker_user: 
     - username: whatever
     - user_id: id_1

when the new broker_link comes
(This happens when the broker_user just changed its username)
broker_user:
    - username: user_b
    - user_id: id_1

[after]
User A
 - username: user_a
 - broker_user: 
     - username: user_b
     - user_id: id_1
 ```
The case 2 makes sure the ID not changed.


### Details

For the case 1 with security concern,

> we should introduce a step during the flow to say "Hey, looks like you have an existing account linked to Foo IdP but using a different than the account you are now authenticating. Do you confirm using the new account instead?"

And make sure the user confirm the override existing broker link.

Introduce a new Authenticator for the first login flow, the process might be:

1. try find the user by `identityProvider` and `brokerUsername`
2. display a confirm screen if exists
3. verify the email by code if user has email (by IdpEmailVerificationAuthenticator)
4. otherwise, we can verify by the credential (by IdpUsernamePasswordForm)
issues.title: Introduce a new Authenticator to handle duplicate IdP broker links

### Description

Currently, when using the SSSD federation provider, if a user that has not logged into keycloak logs in for the first time, their user is imported from SSSD. issues.body:
### Description

This feature request asks to add support for configurable properties to RequiredActions. 
Currently support for configuration of required actions via the admin ui are quite limited. 
The only allowed configuration options are: 
- enabled (is the required action enabled at all?)
- default (is the required action set for new users by default?) 
- order / priority (controls the order in which required actions is presented to the user)

It would be helpful to allow developers to specify additional configurable properties `org.keycloak.provider.ProviderConfigProperty` for required actions, similar to how authenticator executions can be configured.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

Behaviour for required actions should be configurable. Currently one has to pull configuration from realm attributes, env variables or other means.
Having official support for configuration would allow us to have a common way to configure actions. 

### Details

# Implementation ideas

## Configuration options 

There are multiple ways to implement support for configuration options for required actions, here are 2 options:

### Option 1
Leverage `org.keycloak.provider.ProviderFactory#getConfigMetadata()`
Advantages:
- easier, as it is already available API

Disadvantages:
- no default config 
- no help text 

### Option 2
Make required actions infrastructure aware of `org.keycloak.provider.ConfiguredProvider` 
Advantages:
- more options (help text, default config) 
- Developers could opt-in to make their required actions configurable by implementing the `ConfiguredProvider` interface.

Disadvantages:
- a bit more work
- 2 different ways to define config properties (`ProviderFactory#getConfigMetadata()` vs. `ConfiguredProvider#getConfigProperties()`) 

I currently lean toward Option 1.

## Required Action Configuration storage

The required actions infrastructure already supports the persistence of configuration metadata via 
[`org.keycloak.models.jpa.entities.RequiredActionProviderEntity#config`](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/main/model/jpa/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/jpa/entities/RequiredActionProviderEntity.java#L76) in the `REQUIRED_ACTION_CONFIG` table.

## REST API extensions in AuthenticationManagementResource 

The `AuthenticationManagementResource` already supports the management of required actions. It seems as the natural place to add support for required action config management.

I propose to add the following new endpoints to manage required action configuration within a realm bound to the required action "alias" / provider id.
```
  @Path("required-actions/{alias}/config-description")
  @GET
  @Produces(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
  RequiredActionConfigInfoRepresentation getRequiredActionConfigDescription(@PathParam("alias") String alias);

  @Path("required-actions/{alias}/config")
  @GET
  @Produces(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
  RequiredActionConfigRepresentation getRequiredActionConfig(@PathParam("alias") String alias);

  @Path("required-actions/{alias}/config")
  @DELETE
  void removeRequiredActionConfig(@PathParam("alias") String alias);

  @Path("required-actions/{alias}/config")
  @PUT
  @Consumes(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
  void updateRequiredActionConfig(@PathParam("alias") String alias, RequiredActionConfigRepresentation rep);
```

## Additional work
- Introduce RequiredActionConfigModel
- Extend RequiredActionContext to expose RequiredActionConfigModel
- Extend admin-client libraries (jakarta, javaee, js/ts)
- Extend admin ui (required action list with config button and required action config form)
- Update documentation
- Update tests (REST API, UI tests)
issues.title: Make RequiredActions configurable

### Description

The client has expressed the need for organization-specific customization of registration forms within the Keycloak authentication and authorization platform. Presently, Keycloak's registration form settings are managed at the realm level, affecting the entire realm uniformly. In response to this requirement, I propose implementing a mechanism to dynamically generate registration forms tailored to each organization.

Background:
Each client may comprise multiple organizations, with each organization representing distinct groups of users intending to utilize the client application. The current setup lacks granularity, as changes to the registration form apply universally across the realm, irrespective of organizational distinctions.

Proposed Solution:
Customize Registration Flow Based on Organization:
1. Develop functionality to customize the registration form generation process based on the organization.
2. Enable administrators to configure organization-specific registration fields, ensuring flexibility and granularity in form design.

Implementation Plan:
1. Research the feasibility of customizing the registration flow based on organization attributes, such as organization ID or name.
2. Develop custom Keycloak extensions or integrations to interact with the Keycloak API and facilitate dynamic registration form generation.
3. Incorporate administrative controls within Keycloak's interface to manage organization-specific registration field configurations.

Request for Collaboration:
Before proceeding with development, I seek collaboration from the Keycloak community to validate the proposed approach and gather insights on potential challenges or alternative solutions. Your expertise and feedback will contribute to the successful implementation of this enhancement and better address the client's requirements.

Thank you for your support and contributions towards advancing Keycloak's functionality to meet evolving user needs.

It seems that Keycload does not support `id_token_hint`.

I found `id_token_hint` in some places in the code and other places in this repo.
But e.g. this [adoc](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/main/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/sso-protocols/oidc.adoc) says that only login_hint is supported.

Please support `id_token_hint`


### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

Why am I asking about this? I argued in this [project´s IdentityAndConsent WG](https://github.com/camaraproject/IdentityAndConsentManagement) that id_token_hint is superior to login_hint, because the IdP can validate the signature of the id_token and therefore be sure that the sub claim was created by itself, and therefore the sub value is known and understood by the IdP. Somebody countered that keycloak does not support id_token_hint. I would like to kill that argument.


### Details

The straight forward way of implementing id_token_hint in the kc *authorization server* seems to be (happy flow):
- validate the signature of the [id token](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#IDToken)
- take the sub field and treat it like having received that value in the already supported login_hint parameter

Add support here?:

```javascript
        if (options && options.id_token_hint) {
```

Based on the design as specified in #9829.

Add a new command: `kc.sh|bat bootstrap-admin user [--username=value] [--password=value] [--no-prompt] [--expiration=value]`.
* The command works regardless if Keycloak was ever started (and master realm exists), or not.
* If `--username` is not specified, the env variable `KEYCLOAK_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USERNAME` will be checked, if it is not defined, the user will be prompted to enter a username with a default preset to `temp-admin`.
* If `--password` is not specified, the environment variable `KEYCLOAK_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` will be checked, if it is not defined, the user will be prompted for a password.
* If `--no-prompt` is specified, then prompting will not be used. If a value would have required prompting, an error will be shown.
* If the account with the specified username exists an error will be shown.
* `--expiration` specifies the number of minutes after which the account expires. If `--expiration` is not specified, the environment variable `KEYCLOAK_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EXPIRATION` will be checked. Otherwise, the default `120` (2 hours) will be used.

issues.body:
The master realm can be configured to use a passwordless auth flow, or to use some sort of 2nd factor authentication. A simple password recreation such as #29324 would not be enough in those cases. A full recovery process overcomes this by introducing a special auth flow.

The cloud native proposes adding a new kc command, such as “kc.sh recover-admin token [--username=value] [--no-prompt]”. That ccommand generates a JWT token:
* Short lived (5 minutes)
* One time use only
* Signed by master realm key
* Issued for an existing admin user; if it doesn’t exist, creates a new one with specified username

An alternative to a JWT token would be a simple random UUID stored in a database (alongside any metadata like expiration).

The user accesses a special login page meant for admin recovery:
* Served on management interface
  * Possibly on the main HTTP(S) interface to allow easier access via Ingress in K8s environment.
* Is disabled by default
* Handled by a special auth flow.
* Accepts 2 inputs: username and the token that user copy-pasted

Drawbacks:

* Would have the same issues as import / export wrt https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/28384 - https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/29200
* Not great usability when containerized - probably need a cr driven mechanism for triggering the creation of the token, which would then be available via a Secret.

After log in, the user is redirected to the Admin Console.
issues.title: Allow for any admin recovery via a token

issues.body:
### Description

The default discovery protocol provided by Infinispan uses IP multicast (`MPING`) to find its peers in the network. Although it is perfectly fine for an environment with IP multicast available, `JDBC_PING2` seems a better fit as a default discovery protocol for Keycloak. 

The `JDBC_PING2` protocol uses a database to keep track of the peer's IP addresses (and ports) and, we can use the Keycloak database as a registry.

The following work is required:

* Create a custom stack, replacing `MPING` with `JDBC_PING2`
* Infinispan 15.0.3.Final allows injecting a data source into `JDBC_PING2` for Infinispan Server (see https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ISPN-15961). The same code can be used by Keycloak to inject the Quarkus data source into JGroups.
* (UX improvement) Somehow detect the database dialect to configure the `JDBC_PING2` queries (select, delete, insert). The goal is to achieve zero-config for users.
* Set values for remaining options based on user feedback and/or issues found.

`JDBC_PING2` documentation is available here: http://jgroups.org/manual5/index.html#JDBC_PING2

### Discussion

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions/29205

### Issues

_No response_

### Motivation

To simplify Keycloak usage and configuration.

issues.body:
### Description

Make sure that insecure crypto algorithms are not enabled by default when using more strict security profiles. Maybe some might be disabled even with the default security profiles. Maybe it is possible to ensure this by using the client policies, so with more strict client policies, which are enabled when some strict security profile is used, the defaults would be to disable insecure algorithms.

At the same time, we always need to be backwards compatible, so perhaps we will need support for client-policy and client-profiles versioning. Marking as "needs discussion" because of that.

This was originally reported as a bug. The original description is below.



### Describe the bug

While working on #26568 I came to realise we still have some insecure defaults around KC that should really be schedule for sunset.

We should disable insecure use of crypto keys and algorithms  (e.g. the KC side of SAML and OIDC should not support small keys), requiring users to use flags to enable the insecure usage until the functionality is fully sunset.

Non exhaustive list:

-----
- Support for 1024 bits RSA keys. 

  Honestly, it is 2024 and anything below 2048 should not be used, regardless if in government or not. There's barely any up to date software out there that doesn't support larger keys.
  
  The fact is: KC is a security service, supporting 1024 bit keys should not be an offer that is in place anymore. NIST has been recommending 2048 since 2015 [(NIST SP 800-57 Part 3 Rev. 1)](https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.800-57pt3r1). Even the Zulu JDK clearly states: 
  
> uses a 1024-bit RSA key which is considered a security risk. This key size will be disabled in a future update

![image](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/assets/3108527/b280edd0-6728-4ae0-ba8c-3b38830d8fe9)

-----
- Support for PKCS 1.5, the basis for rs256

  Due to [NIST SP 800-131A Revision 2](https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.800-131Ar2) guidance around RSA PKCS 1.5, [OpenSSL](https://github.com/openssl/project/issues/241) is planning to handle its deprecation.
  
  Meanwhile BC-FIPS already informed users [that it's FIPS 140-3 compliant TLS will not support it](https://github.com/bcgit/bc-java/issues/1529#issuecomment-1798435148). It is unclear if the non TLS stack will support it. 
  
  If that is not enough, PKCS 1.5 is hasn't been recommended since [at least 2020](https://www.scottbrady91.com/jose/jwts-which-signing-algorithm-should-i-use). 
  
  On its [Open Banking page HSBC states](https://develop.hsbc.com/knowledge-article/api-authentication-and-digital-signature-e2e-trust-token):

### Description

Based on the design as specified in https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/9829.

Add a new command: `kc.sh|bat bootstrap-admin service [--client-id=value] [--secret=value] [--no-prompt] [--expiration=value]`.
* The command works regardless if Keycloak was ever started (and master realm exists), or not.
* If `--client-id` is not specified, the env variable `KEYCLOAK_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_CLIENT_ID` will be checked, if it is not defined, the user will be prompted to enter a Client ID with a default preset to `temp-admin-service`.
* If `--secret` is not specified, the environment variable `KEYCLOAK_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET` will be checked, if not defined, the user will be prompted for a secret.
* If `--no-prompt` is specified, then prompting will not be used. If a value would have required prompting, an error will be shown.
* If the Client with the specified Client ID exists an error will be shown.
* `--expiration` specifies the number of minutes after which the Client expires. If `--expiration` is not specified, the environment variable `KEYCLOAK_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EXPIRATION` will be checked. Otherwise, the default `120` (2 hours) will be used.

Based on the provided arguments, a Client is created in the master Realm with the following specifications:
* It has all flows disabled.
* The Client requires authentication.
* Service account is enabled.
* The service account has the admin Realm Role assigned.
issues.title: Bootstrapping an admin service account using a dedicated command

### Description

This top-level epic is about the planned work to deliver the first release of the Keycloak Organization feature.

Keycloak Organization is a feature that leverages and builds on top of the Identity and Access Management (IAM) capabilities of Keycloak to address Customer Identity and Access Management (CIAM) with a focus on Business-to-Business (B2B) use cases.

                                        +-----------+                  
                                        |           |                  
                            +-----------+  Customer +-----------+      
                            |           |           |           |      
    +----------+      +-----+----+      |           |      +----+-----+
    |          |      |          |      +-----------+      |          |
    | End-User +------+  Realm   |                         | End-User |
    |          |      |          |                         |          |
    |          |      |          |                         |          |
    +----------+      +-----+----+                         +----+-----+
                            |           +-----------+           |      
                            |           |           |           |      
                            +-----------+  Partner  +-----------+      
                                        |           |                  
                                        |           |                  
                                        +-----------+                       

In summary, this feature will allow a realm to integrate with third-party entities like customers and business partners so that their identities and how they access protected resources at the realm level are segregated and managed within the scope of the organization they belong to. 

As a result, a realm will be able to provide a different experience when onboarding customer identities or identities from a business partner and mechanisms to secure and manage how they interact with a realm and how they access protected resources from the clients available from a realm. Although not the main focus, it should also be possible to leverage this feature if you just want a better segregation between users, clients, and how they are managed and authenticate to a realm—some level of multi-tenancy.

The main set of capabilities provided by Keycloak Organizations are:

* * [x] **Manage Organizations**
* * [x] **Manage Organization Members**
* * * [x] Organization Member Self-Registration based on Identity Brokering
* * * [x] Organization Member Registration based on Invitation Links
* * * [x] [Manage Invitations](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/38809)
* * * [x] [Joining Multiple Organizations](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/29613) 
* * [ ] **Manage Federated Organization Members**
* * * [ ] [Managing members from LDAP](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/37401)
* * * [ ] [Managing members for custom user storage providers](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/37405)
* * [x] **Mapping organization metadata in tokens** 
* * [x] **[Customizing templates based on organizations](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/30313)**
* * [ ] [**Manage Organization Roles**](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/40585)
* * [x] [**Manage Organization Groups**](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/43507)
* * [ ] **Manage Groups of Organizations**
* * [ ] **Manage Authentication within the Scope of an Organization**
* * * [ ] Authentication based on the Organization Authentication Policies
* * [ ] **Manage Clients and Service Accounts**
* * [x] **Administrative Authorization**
* * * [x] [**RBAC**](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/45497)
* * * [x] [**Fine-Grained**](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/47284) 
* * [ ] **Organization-specific Admin and User Events**
* * [ ] **Support for synchronizing identities from organizations using SCIM**
* * [ ] **Organization Self-Service**

The planned release dates for Keycloak Organization are:

| Release  | Scope | State |
| ------------- | ------------- | ------------- |
| 25.0.0  |#28609| Preview  |
| 26.0.0  |#30229 | Supported  |

For more details about the release dates, see https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/milestones.

### Discussion

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions/23948

### Issues
