- [x] [Keycloak Organizations fully supported](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/30229)

### Motivation

Keycloak is a well-known open-source IAM solution and we want to leverage now its capabilities to enable CIAM with a focus on B2B use cases.

issues.body:
### Description

Putting an additional claim to an exchanged token in Token Exchange.

Current protocol mappers are applied to an exchanged token (to internal) in Token Exchange.
However, these protocol mappers are applied not only an access token by Token Response in any kind of grant, but applied in Token Exchange.

Therefore, current protocol mappers are not applied to only an exchanged token in Token Exchange.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

This feature is beneficial for a use case where a keycloak user only put some specific claim to an exchanged token in only Token Exchange. For example, in micro-service architecture applied environment, a claim that can be meaningful for some workload inside microservices should be put onto only an exchanged token, not onto an access token outside microservices.

### Details

AFAIK, there are two ways to realize it;
1. Enhance existing protocol mappers 
2. Created new types of protocol mappers
3. Using client policies

As for 1, we add a switch to existing protocol mappers. If the switch is ON, it is applied to an exchanged token in Token Exchange. If OFF, it is not applied.

Advantage: 
- We need not to modify existing Token Exchange source code.

Disadvantage: 
- It needs some migration mechanism.
- We need to control UI to show the switch only if keycloak runs with Token Exchange feature.
- One additional switch is shown in Admin UI, which complicates operations by a keycloak's admin.
- The protocol mapper is applied to an exchanged token in every patterns of Token Exchange. For example, there are two patters of Token Exchange (A and B), then, the protocol mapper is applied to an exchanged token in Token Exchange pattern A, and Token Exchange pattern B.

As for 2, we add new type of a protocol mapper `TokenExchangeMapper` like `OID4VCMapper` in OID4VCI. This protocol mapper is only applied to an exchanged token in Token Exchange.

Advantage: 
- It need not some migration mechanism.

Disadvantage: 
- We need to modify existing Token Exchange source code.
- The protocol mapper is applied to an exchanged token in every patterns of Token Exchange. For example, there are two patters of Token Exchange (A and B), then, the protocol mapper is applied to an exchanged token in Token Exchange pattern A, and Token Exchange pattern B.

As for 3, we use client policies to add some claims to an exchanged token in Token Exchange

Advantage:
- It need not some migration mechanism.
- It can change which claims are put onto to an exchanged token in each patterns of Token Exchange. For example, there are two patters of Token Exchange (A and B), then, the client policy's executor put a claim X to an exchanged token in Token Exchange pattern A, while the other client policy's executor put a claim Y to an exchanged token in Token Exchange pattern B.

Disadvantage:
- We need not to modify existing Token Exchange source code for applying client policies in Token Exchange (current Keycloak does not apply client policies in Token Exchange)
issues.title: Add claims to an exchanged token in Token Exchange

Hi, I'm Harshita. I’m working with [CNCF and the Google Open Source Security Team for the GSoC 2024 term](https://github.com/cncf/mentoring/issues/1196). We are collaborating to enhance security practices across various CNCF projects. The goal is to improve security for all CNCF projects by both using OpenSSF Scorecards and implementing its security improvements.

The [Open Source Security Foundation](https://openssf.org/) (OpenSSF) [Scorecard](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard) is a tool designed to evaluate the security posture of open-source projects. This has the [Scorecard GitHub Action](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard-action), which automates the process by running security checks on the GitHub repository. By integrating this Action into the repository's workflow, developers can continuously monitor the project’s security posture. The Scorecard checks cover various security best practices and provide scores for multiple categories. Some checks include Code Reviews, Branch Protection, Signed Releases, etc.

The workflow runs on every change in the main branch. It publishes the Scorecard checks' results to the project's security dashboard and includes suggestions on how to solve any issues. This Action has already been adopted by 1800+ projects, with prominent users like [Tensorflow](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow), [Angular](https://github.com/angular/angular), [sos.dev](http://sos.dev/), [deps.dev](http://deps.dev/), and many CNCF projects.

Once the Scorecard GitHub Action is set up and running, the results can be displayed as a badge in the repository's README file. This badge serves as a quick indicator of the project's security posture, helping users and contributors evaluate the project's security practices quickly.

The OpenSSF Scorecard improves open-source project's security by providing automated, transparent assessments of their security practices. - Username and password (required)
```
- MFA (required subflow)
  - OTP Form (alternative)
  - WebAuthn Authenticator (alternative)
```

### Discussion

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions/14988

### Motivation

Currently Keycloak supports having alternative MFA options (e.g., OTP and WebAuthn), but as far as I can tell there is no support to allow configuring one of the options on the first login. A workaround, mentioned in the linked discussion is to have one of the MFA options as a "Required" step in an "Alternative" subflow, e.g.:
```
- MFA (required subflow)
  - TOTP (alternative subflow)
    - OTP Form (required)
  - WebAuthn Authenticator (alternative)
```

In this case, users are presented with the first configured MFA option from the alternatives, and if no MFA token is configured, they are asked to configure an OTP. While this approach works, it does not provide the option to configure the WebAuthn token as the first (and maybe only) token.

### Details

Authentication steps that can be configured (e.g., HOTP / TOTP, WebAuthn, email OTP?) should provide the option to set them up on the first login, so users can configure the token and proceed with the login afterwards, instead of failing the login flow.

The administration console should provide the option to configure the steps as "can be set up as first token", since not all options may be equally applicable for all users (e.g., we can assume users have a computer or phone they can use to generate TOTPs, but FIDO tokens are rather expensive, so they are only used by a small subset of users); if some of the options are not configurable as the first token, they should be available in the account console, but not on the first login screen.
issues.title: Allow users to select MFA configuration options from alternatives on first login

Currently we support user lookups by username or email, but in many scenarios involving mobile phones a username or email address is not available to lookup a user, but the phonenumber is. issues.body:
### Description

Since Keycloak is not yet supporting [Rich Authorization Request (RAR)](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9396), we are using a custom protocol mapper in order to include `authorization_details` in issued tokens, when using a [Pushed Authorization Request (PAR)](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9126) flow. This was also recommended in [discussions/22991](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions/22991).
This is possible because the [ParEndpoint](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/25.0.4/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/par/endpoints/ParEndpoint.java) processing goes through [AuthorizationEndpoint.java#L332](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/25.0.4/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/endpoints/AuthorizationEndpoint.java#L332), that stores any additional request parameters in client session notes, which can then be accessed from a custom protocol mapper.

However, we also need RAR for a client grant type token. But since the [TokenEndpoint](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/25.0.4/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/endpoints/TokenEndpoint.java) processing does not store the additional request parameters, we cannot use the custom protocol mapper to achieve RAR in this case.

Therefore, we are requesting that additional request parameters is stored as notes on either the user or client session when processing a client grant type request in order to enable RAR for client grant tokens via a custom protocol mapper.

### Motivation

Among others, [EU digital wallet framework (ARF)](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/blob/main/docs/arf.md) uses [Cloud Signature Consortium (CSC) API v2](https://cloudsignatureconsortium.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/csc-api-v2.0.0.2.pdf), which requires the use of [RAR](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9396).

Furthermore, the Japanese government agency [Digital Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Agency) is standardizing based on CSC v2, meaning they are also closely following eiDAS 2 and ARF.

While it is our impression that Keycloak will eventually fully support RAR per default, this feature request would enable RAR compatibility via a custom protocol mapper in the meantime.

### Details

My implementation idea would be to add something similar to [AuthorizationEndpoint.java#L332](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/25.0.4/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/endpoints/AuthorizationEndpoint.java#L332) here: [ClientCredentialsGrantType.java#L130](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/25.0.4/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/ClientCredentialsGrantType.java#L130)

It would perhaps need a similar method to [extractAdditionalReqParams](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/25.0.4/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/endpoints/request/AuthzEndpointRequestParser.java#L127), in order not to store all the `formParams` but only the "additional" parameters.
issues.title: Enabling authorization_details for client grant tokens until RAR is fully implemented

issues.body:
### Description

This feature is fully implemented in Keycloak but it is disabled due to performance and a bug present in Infinispan `15.0.8.Final` and older. At the time of writing, Infinispan `15.0.10.Final` is out and testing can be resumed. 

The main motivation behind this is performance. Infinispan is faster for accessing the sessions, mainly because it stores the data in memory. The data is safe if a single cluster crashes since the other site retains a copy of the data. If all Infinispan clusters are down, the data is lost. This is the disadvantage when compared with the persistent sessions feature: the data survives even if the database crashes on both sites.

Coding is completed, but documentation and testing need to be completed. This epic tracks the missing work.

### Feedback!

Please provide feedback on this epic or in the discussion https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions/33745

### Use cases and drawbacks.

User and client sessions are important depending on the deployment requirements. For some deployments, sessions must not be lost at any cost, and storing them in the database is the strongest guarantee provided by Keycloak. However, storing the sessions in an in-memory database is a fine solution for less strict requirements and provides a better system performance overall. 

**Warning**: Data loss may occur with volatile sessions. By default, two copies of the data exist in the Infinispan cluster, supporting a single node failure. The number of copies can be increased in the cache configuration and the write operation will become more expensive. Shutting down all the nodes in the clusters incurs full data loss.

### Multi-Site setup

**Deploy Infinispan with the Infinispan Operator**

The guide [Deploy Infinispan for HA with the Infinispan Operator](https://www.keycloak.org/high-availability/deploy-infinispan-kubernetes-crossdc) is a good starting point. Follow the steps until you reach section `6 Creating the caches for Keycloak`. The caches need to be configured as shown in the following Gist:

https://gist.github.com/pruivo/94a93c91afc162cb00b426ed54f25154

**Deploy Keycloak with the Keycloak Operator**

The Keycloak configuration changes are minimal. Following the guide [Deploy Keycloak for HA with the Keycloak Operator](https://www.keycloak.org/high-availability/deploy-keycloak-kubernetes), the only changes are the enabled features. The `persistent-user-session` feature must be disabled; `clusterless` and `multi-site` must be enabled. In the end, it looks as follows:

```yaml
  features:
    enabled:
      - multi-site
      - clusterless
    disabled:
      - persistent-user-sessions
```

### Single-Site setup

**Deploy Infinispan with the Infinispan Operator**

The guide [Deploy Infinispan for HA with the Infinispan Operator](https://www.keycloak.org/high-availability/deploy-infinispan-kubernetes-crossdc) is a good starting point. The following steps can be skipped since they are irrelevant for single-site deployment:

3. Create a service account.
4. Create TLS secrets

The remaining steps need to be adapted as follows

5. Create a Cluster for Infinispan

The Infinispan CR for single-site deployments is as follows.

```yaml
apiVersion: infinispan.org/v1
kind: Infinispan
metadata:
  name: infinispan 
  namespace: keycloak
  annotations:
    infinispan.org/monitoring: 'true' 
spec:
  replicas: 3
  security:
    endpointSecretName: connect-secret 
  service:
    type: DataGrid
```

6. Creating the caches for Keycloak

The caches need to be configured as shown in the following Gist:

https://gist.github.com/pruivo/94a93c91afc162cb00b426ed54f25154

**Deploy Keycloak with the Keycloak Operator**

The Keycloak configuration changes are minimal. Following the guide [Deploy Keycloak for HA with the Keycloak Operator](https://www.keycloak.org/high-availability/deploy-keycloak-kubernetes), the only changes are the enabled features. The `persistent-user-session` feature must be disabled; `clusterless` must be enabled. In the end, it looks as follows:

```yaml
  features:
    enabled:
      - clusterless
    disabled:
      - persistent-user-sessions
```

```[tasklist]
### Tasks
- [ ] https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/32270
- [ ] https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak-benchmark/pull/971
- [ ] https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/33646
- [ ] https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak-benchmark/issues/1013
- [ ] Multi-site volatile: document how to enable indexing in the external Infinispan cluster
```

issues.body:
### Description

Creating and managing clients in Keycloak today can be a daunting task. There are two particularly big reasons for this:

1. Lack of any specific type for a client. A client is either an OpenID Connect or SAML client. However, there are many different types of clients that use a given protocol. For example a single-page app, a REST API, or a service account.
2. Lack of any versioning around clients results in it being hard to change default behaviour, and often requiring introducing backwards compatibility flags on clients when changes happen

To expand on 1. when creating a client through the Admin UI the user is presented with a huge-range of options, many of which are often not applicable to the type being created. As an example when creating a service account you would follow these steps:

a. Create new client
b. Select `OpenID Connect` as the `Client type` and add a `Client ID` (Always display in UI is not relevant in this case)
c. Click next
d. Enable `Client authentication` and disable all flows except `Service account roles`
e. Click next

Now the service account is created, but there is a lot of options available that is not relevant to a service account, some examples including:

Root URL, Home URL, Admin URL
Always display in UI
Login and logout settings
Keys (actually not sure when this is applicable?)
Client scopes
Sessions (client credential grant doesn't create sessions)
A lot of options under advanced
By introducing client types as a first-class citizen it would be possible to create a more specific type of client, without irrelevant options available in Admin UI or APIs. It would also make it easier to filter clients by type.

Versioning of client types are also an important aspect. A client can for example be of type `oidc:v1`, which means that it can rely on the protocol, and claims/assertions to be backward compatible. At the same time `oidc:v2` can be introduced with different behaviour when needed.

### Discussion

### Motivation

### Details

issues.body:
### Description

Hello Keycloak team,

I would like to propose a new feature for Keycloak: support for the request_uri parameter in the OpenID Connect Identity Provider configuration.

Context:
I am using Keycloak to secure a Spring application, and I have integrated an OIDC-compliant Authorization Server as an Identity Provider (OpenID Connect v1.0). The discovery process successfully sets up the required endpoints, and I have configured client authentication with "JWT signed with private key," including the necessary scopes and other relevant data.

However, my use case requires sending a request_uri during the authorization request, as outlined in the OpenID Connect Core specification: https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#UseRequestUri.

The well-known configuration of the Authorization Server indicates that "request_uri_parameter_supported": true, but currently, there is no option in Keycloak to configure this parameter in the Identity Provider settings.

Feature Request:
Adding support for the request_uri parameter (or alternatively, the request parameter for JWT by value) in the OpenID Connect authorization flow would enhance the flexibility and security of Keycloak's integrations with third-party OIDC providers. This feature is particularly useful when dealing with identity providers that require passing additional parameters securely or managing dynamic client registration.

Why this feature is important:
Enhanced Security: The request_uri and request parameters allow for secure transmission of additional request parameters as part of the authorization flow, reducing the risk of query parameter tampering and providing stronger guarantees of integrity.

Compliance with OIDC Standards: Many OIDC-compliant Authorization Servers already support this feature (indicated in their well-known configuration). By supporting this feature, Keycloak can maintain full compatibility with the OpenID Connect Core specification and ensure interoperability with more identity providers.

Dynamic Request Customization: This would also allow Keycloak administrators to pass complex and secure request objects in scenarios where direct query parameter passing is insufficient. This flexibility is essential in cases where identity providers enforce strict security policies around request validation.

Expected Behavior:
A configuration option in the Identity Provider settings to enable the use of request_uri, allowing administrators to pass a URI that points to a JWT containing request parameters.

### Description

Suppose we create two groups in a Keycloak realm: `group1` and `group2`.  For each of these groups, we add an attribute `attr`.

Group 1 assigns the value `value1` to `attr`:

![grp1](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b49548e0-80a6-45d6-9568-fde2673d6fc0)

Group 2 assigns the value `value2` to `attr`:

![grp2](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f4738011-b371-45ff-96a0-fbe54bb3f687)

Next, we add a user to both groups.  In a client, we then create a User Attribute mapper to map the value of `attr` to a token claim:

![mapper](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bd893271-b07c-497d-976e-ee4c3aa7318a)

As of Keycloak 26.0.5, it's not clear -- and doesn't seem to be consistent -- which value of `attr` will be assigned to a user that belongs to both groups.  I have experimented with various combinations of adding/removing the user from the groups, deleting and recreating the groups, etc.  Maybe I'm missing something obvious, but I can't seem to discern the logic used to determine the value applied to the user via the mapper.

I would suggest that group and role attributes should have a priority value that could be used to determine order of precedence when one has attributes of the same name.

If this functionality already exists and I have somehow missed it, I apologize.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

It would be ideal if we had a priority value associated with attributes so that one group/role could override the value of an attribute also found in other groups/roles.

Here's a real-world example.  We have deployed NextCloud, which can use an OIDC claim `nextCloudQuota` to determine a user's quota.  I have an LDAP mapper that maps Active Directory groups to Keycloak groups when a user logs in:

`NextCloud-Users`
`NextCloud-Admins`

I then associate different values for `nextCloudQuota` to the two groups.

Now, an admin will be a member of both groups -- but we want the value of `nextCloudQuota` associated with the `NextCloud-Admins` group to take precedence for anyone that belongs to that group.

If there was a priority value for the attributes, I could assign a higher priority for the `nextCloudQuota` attribute associated with the `NextCloud-Admins` group vs. the `NextCloud-Users` group.

### Details

For each attribute, instead of just name and value, I would propose to have name, value, and priority.  If an attribute of the same name is applied by multiple groups or roles, the value with the highest priority is then applied to the user.
issues.title: Add a Priority Value to Group and Role Attributes

issues.body:
### Description

A frequent way to configure logging is with some default logging set in environment variables or in `keycloak.conf`, or of course just through `--log-level`.

However, at times you want to quickly and easily increase logging for a specific category; for example enable debug for `org.keycloak.cookie` if you are having some issues with cookies.

If you only use `--log-level` to configure logging that works fine, as you can specify the `log-level` option multiple times:
```
--log-level=WARN,org.keycloak:INFO --log-level=org.keycloak.cookie:DEBUG`
```

In `keycloak.conf` and with environment variables this doesn't work as you can only have a single value. 

For `keycloak.conf` sure you can extend on the `log-level` option to add all categories, but this is inconvenient if you just want to quickly add debug for a single category. 

For environment variables you could of course do something like ```KC_LOG_LEVEL=$KC_LOG_LEVEL,org.keycloak.cookie:DEBUG```, but that's also somewhat inconvinient.

The bigger problem though is if you use multiple source for configuration. Perhaps you have `keycloak.conf` with some default logging config, but then want to use environment variables at times. When doing this you have to take the default config from `keycloak.conf` and add it to the environment variable.

A much more convenient approach would be to also support specific options for individual categories:

```
KC_LOG_CATEGORY__ORG_KEYCLOAK_COOKIE__LEVEL=DEBUG
log-category-"org.keycloak.cookie"-level=DEBUG
```

This would make it a lot more convinient to quickly bump logging for a specific category.

If there is conflicts between `log-level` and the category specific levels, then the latter should take precedence. 

### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

_No response_

### Details

_No response_
issues.title: Ability to specify log category levels through separate options

issues.body:
### Description

The customer has a business requirement to take certain actions if users are not configured for 2FA. They are looking to perform an authentication Flow that uses this condition to detect if a user does not have any 2FA method.

### Possible solution

The easiest approach is to implement the option `Negate output` in the condition `Condition - User configured` . The option `Negate output` is available for example in the `Condition - user role` .

Currently the `Condition - User configured` evaluates to true if at least one of the 2-factor authenticators configured in the related conditional subflow is present. So when added `Negate output` option, it will allow to have subflow, which will evaluate to true just if NONE of the configured 2-factor authenticators from the same subflow is present.

Together with the `Deny Access` authenticator, this can be used to achieve the requirement. As for example it may be possible to configure the authentication flow with the subflows like these:

```
- (All other authenticators like cookie, password etc)
- Subflow1 - 2factor enabled
  - Condition - user configured (Negate output = false)
  - OTP ALTERNATIVE
  - WebAuthn ALTERNATIVE
  - Recovery codes ALTERNATIVE
- Subflow2 - 2factor disabled
  - Condition - user configured (Negate output = true)
  - Deny Access ALTERNATIVE
  - OTP ALTERNATIVE
  - WebAuthn ALTERNATIVE
  - Recovery codes ALTERNATIVE 
```

This will allow to authenticate users with 2-factor configured (subflow1), but reject authentication for users without 2-factor configured (subflow2).

It is possible that some other adjustements may be needed in the implementation of `ConditionalUserConfiguredAuthenticator` to make this happen or configure the `subflow2` in slightly different way. But hopefully some setup like this may work. Will need further investigation...

The disadvantage is the need of duplication of all the 2-factor authenticators in both subflows and the complication of such a setup. The better will be to have authentication policies, which would allow better achieve something like this more easily. But that is for the future though...

### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

_No response_

### Details

_No response_
issues.title: Ability to reject authentication to users without 2FA configured

issues.body:
The aim of this task is to improve support for configuring permissions for token exchange.

Currently it is possible to configure with fine-grained admin permissions that client `client-a` is able to exchange token with the audience `target` . 

It will be good to have also those abilities, which are not supported right now.
- Restrict based on scopes (EG. token exchange is permitted just if scopes `scope-a` or `scope-b` is requested, but not `scope-c`)
- Restrict based on token types (EG. token exchange allowed just if access token requested, but not when refresh-token requested)
- based on types of requester or target client (allow/not-allow for public clients)
- based on whether it is client has consent required
- based on whether "delegation" is needed
- More?

Right now, it is possible to configure policies on target/audience client side (EG. Group of clients, which is able to pass authorization policy `X` is able to exchange for audience `target`), but it is not possible to exchange on "requester" client side (EG. group of target clients, which can pass authorization policy `Y` can be exchanged as audience from requester client `client-a`).


### Notes

- This task might be probably divided into multiple subtasks and multiple PRs. Just using this as "umbrella" for now. Maybe converted to epic?

- Some use-cases for permissions are described in [this document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1T_4hjf0tapLAC5Hpac8wNiEHcrAmYZDQGpj3JRJ2MBI/edit?tab=t.0)

- We may need to add some additional data to be available to authorization policies. Some additional attributes (like `TokenExchangeContext`, parsed tokens etc) can be added to `EvaluationContext` somewhere [here](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/26.0.6/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissions.java#L365)

- Not 100% sure if we need 2 calls for authorization-services (one for check `target` client as it is now and another for check requester client like `client-a`), but not 100% sure yet... The check for "requester" client is possibly not strictly needed in 26.2, but could be added as a follow-up (TBD)

- There will be new admin UI and configuration for fine-grained admin permissions. This is being done by core-iam and UI teams and it is not part of this task.

- New implementation of some authorization policies may be needed. Question here is, if we can have single implementation (like `TokenExchangeAuthorizationPolicy`) with all the configuration on the single place like on the picture below or if we want dedicated policy implementations for various things (scopes, requested token types, consent etc) and then "aggregate" them. IMO single implementation might be better and easier for administrators to configure for token-exchange, but might be subject for discussions...

![Screenshot from 2024-11-28 11-52-35](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0e67ad89-eaa9-4c6a-8a70-4b4dbbb13427)

Additionally, anyone that wants to stay on the latest and greatest would need to bump all feature versions.

We should consider introducing something like `--feature=compatible|latest|preview`, where:

issues.body:
### Description

Add support for specifying a DN of a reverse proxy when mTLS is used for communication between Keycloak and the reverse proxy.
* Add a new server level option for that. Suggested candidate for a name is `proxy-trusted-dn`
* If configured, Keycloak needs to drop all requests that _appear_ to be coming from a reverse proxy
  * This concerns requests that contain (X-)Forwarded headers (depending on the value of the `proxy-headers` option) or client cert lookup header (the `spi-x509cert-lookup-<provider>-ssl-client-cert` option).
  * The request should be dropped even in case when `https-client-auth=request` and mTLS is not used for current request.
* The options can be specified only if all of the following conditions are met.
  * `proxy-headers` option is specified.
  * `https-client-auth` is set to `request` or `required`.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

#### Proxy authentication

Reverse proxy can set various security sensitive aspects of a request, such as client IP address (which is then reflected in brute force detection) or even [client certificate for X.509 authentication](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/6f469b9dd19d49cf4ee7f4067ca9ce7db5927652/docs/guides/server/reverseproxy.adoc?plain=1#L162-L177). Typically, the proxy sets specific HTTP headers to do that. However, the headers can be set by whatever is able to make requests to Keycloak. If the network is misconfigured, an attacker is able to make requests that look like they are coming from a proxy. Hence some sort of "proxy authentication" is required to make Keycloak trust that given proxy request is really coming from a proxy.

We currently have `proxy-trusted-addresses` option for that but it'd be good to provide additional and more secure mechanism.

#### Keeping support for backchannel requests

Keycloak currently allows specifying a specific trustore for mTLS via the `https-trust-store-*` options which is independent from the [system truststore](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/6f469b9dd19d49cf4ee7f4067ca9ce7db5927652/docs/guides/server/keycloak-truststore.adoc?plain=1#L13-L25). However this is not enough for the proxy authentication as there might be backchannel requests that also use mTLS. So we need to be able to differentiate between proxy requests and other requests that might also be using mTLS.

### Details

* Given we need to consider custom proxy headers (specified via the `spi-x509cert-lookup-<provider>-ssl-client-cert` option), probably doesn't make much sense to be implemented at Quarkus level.
* We could create a filter in Keycloak to reject the identified requests.
issues.title: DN validation of reverse proxy

issues.body:
### Description

In the context of rolling upgrades, this new CLI command will have the goal of checking if two configurations are backward compatible. A backward compatible configuration means that Keycloak servers running these two configurations are valid and do not break any logic.

An example of a backward incompatible configuration is the feature `persistent-user-sessions`. If in the same clusters, some servers have this feature enabled and others disabled, the sessions will be broken: some nodes will store sessions in memory while others in the database. 

A backward compatible configuration change is `--cache-embedded-authorization-max-count`. This option is local to the node and does not affect the logic. Servers with different values will work just fine. 

The command `update-compatibility` will be divided into two subcommands:

* `save`: stores the relevant configuration in a JSON file. 
* `check`: check if the current configuration is compatible with one stored in a JSON file.

In the context of this issue, the JSON file will contain only the Keycloak and Infinispan versions, and make a decision based on this limited information. In the future, the JSON will be extended to include all the relevant options. 

### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

_No response_

### Details

The `check` exit code will signal if the configuration is compatible. It is easier for the Keycloak operator and for further user scripts to check the exit code than parsing logs from the server:

**Exit code:**
* 0: Rolling upgrade possible.
* 1: Error (of any kind). 
* 2: Wrong CLI parameters.
* 3: Rolling upgrade NOT possible, the cluster must be shut down before applying the new configuration.

If not compatible, logs will disclose what option.

Usage Example
* `./kc.sh update-compatibility save --features=A --output=/path/to/file.json`
* `./kc.sh update-compatibility check --features=B --input=/path/to/file.json`
issues.title: New CLI command: update-compatibility

### Description

Introduce a new spec in the Keycloak CR to configure the upgrade strategy.

```yaml
upgrade:
  strategy: Auto|Rolling|Recreate|<none>
```

The spec will be under the `unsupported` section for Keycloak 26.2 until we are more confident.

| Option | Description |
|--------|--------|
| `<none>` | Keep the default behavior as in Keycloak 26 - scale down the stateful set if the image changes |
| `Recreate` | Scales down the stateful set if the image or configuration changes | 
| `Rolling` | If a rolling upgrade is possible (zero downtime upgrade), automatically update the stateful set; otherwise wait for use input to perform a `Recreate` upgrade strategy | 
| `Auto` | Automatic performs a `Rolling` or `Recreate` upgrade based on the configuration changes |

issues.body:
### Description

The previous issue [issues/34146](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/34146) was closed due to inactivity, but it is still important for us to find a solution to this.

If it is too "breaking" for now, would you consider a solution that takes the token type from a configuration instead? Like you have done for Verifiable Credentials: [oid4vc/issuance/signing/SigningProperties.java#L37](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/26.1.0/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oid4vc/issuance/signing/SigningProperties.java#L37)

Or adding a feature flag to be able to set this value until another solution has been implemented.

This issue is quite important to us. We would be grateful if we can find a solution. Thank you in advance.

----

**Original description:**

As described in https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions/8646#discussioncomment-10485823:

According to [rfc9068#section-2.1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9068#section-2.1):

> JWT access tokens MUST include this media type in the "typ" header parameter

It then says:

> it is RECOMMENDED that the "application/" prefix be omitted. Therefore, the "typ" value used SHOULD be "at+jwt".

Therefore, it is not just a recommendation, but a requirement that the typ header is either application/at+jwt or at+jwt.
From these two choices, the recommended one is at+jwt.

There is already a switch in [DefaultTokenManager.java#L239](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/26.0.1/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/jose/jws/DefaultTokenManager.java#L239) on the token category to set a specific type for logout tokens.

Could we extend this with a case for the ACCESS category? There is already a constant defined for at+jwt in [TokenUtil.java#L46](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/26.0.1/core/src/main/java/org/keycloak/util/TokenUtil.java#L46).
issues.title: Support token type "at+jwt" for OAuth 2 access tokens

### Description

CockroachDB is a widely adopted, scalable alternative to AWS Aurora, designed for multi-cloud and private cloud environments. A comparison between the two can be found [here](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/compare/amazon-aurora-vs-cockroachdb/). Given its capabilities, CockroachDB is increasingly being used by organisations that require a high-availability and scalable PostgreSQL-compatible database.

For several years, PhaseTwo has successfully provided CockroachDB support for Keycloak, serving multiple clients in production, including deployments managing up to 20 million users. Additionally, many community members are leveraging their open-source distribution ( https://quay.io/repository/phasetwo/keycloak-crdb?tab=tags) (~1000+ pulls/day) independently, demonstrating the demand and viability of CockroachDB as a backend for Keycloak.

Keycloak is often a mission-critical service, where high availability and scalability are essential. Upstream support for CockroachDB would empower organisations seeking a resilient and scalable database option while fostering broader experimentation within the community.To advance this effort, PhaseTwo has offered to contribute CockroachDB support upstream, ensuring that more Keycloak users can experiment with it main distribution. If the community feedback is positive, this can pave the way for further maturity and long-term support.

**Key Benefits for the Keycloak Project & Community**
Scalability & High Availability: CockroachDB offers strong resilience, making it ideal for large-scale Keycloak deployments.
Expanded Deployment Options: Supports organisations looking for a cloud-agnostic, distributed SQL database.
Community-Driven Improvement: Enables broader adoption and validation within the Keycloak ecosystem.
This contribution aligns with the open-source ethos and provides Keycloak users with greater flexibility in database selection.

Since Keycloak already accommodates options like AWS Aurora and others, it might be worthwhile for the Keycloak team to contemplate including experimental support for CockroachDB as well. issues.body:
### Description

Keycloak does not currently provide any mechanisms to automatically disable or remove users. There are a number of use-cases where this is relevant:

* Automatically disable dormant users
* Automatically delete abandoned users
* Transient/temporary users brokered from identity providers
* Transient/temporary users federated through user federation providers

This is relevant to PIP (for example GDPR) where it is generally a requirement to not store user information when not needed.

This is an alternative proposal to transient users for brokering. Transient users stored in sessions is not a solution to privacy for many reasons; sessions may still be persisted to the database, they may be long lived; and additionally and probably the biggest issue from a privacy perspective there is no mechanism to identity user information stored in transient user sessions, so there may be long-lived and persisted sessions storing information about users. From a privacy perspective users have the right to know what information is stored about them, as well as a right to have their information deleted from a provider; neither of which can be guaranteed with transient user sessions.

### Value Proposition
Automatically disabling and/or deletion of user accounts provides increased security (unused and no longer maintained accounts can be abused) and privacy (not storing user information when no longer needed).

### Goals
* Ability to automatically disable unused users after a configurable time
* Ability to automatically delete unused users after a configurable time
* Ability to automatically delete users from a identity provider where there are no active sessions
* Ability to automatically delete users from a federation provider where there are no active sessions
* Remove experimental transient user stored in user sessions

### Non-Goals
* Not importing users coming from an identity provider into LDAP. Ability to selectively add users to a federation provider is not covered by this issue, and would be a separate RFE.
issues.title: Automatic deletion and disabling of users

### Description

Currently, when you link an Identity Provider to an Organization, it becomes unavailable for other Organizations or users that are not a member of any Organization. I believe Keycloak either shouldn't be disabling the provider elsewhere, or having the ability to flag the identity provider as shared in someway should be possible.


### Discussion

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions/37821

### Motivation

We offer Microsoft and Google social login. Currently some of our customer's organizations users have signed in with the the social provider, and others used built in account.

Some customers are now wanting to mandate Google or Microsoft based logins for their users onto our platform. If I tie our existing Microsoft/Google Identity Provider to their Organization, it becomes unavailable for other organizations and for non-organization users.

If I need to add duplicate Identity Providers for Google/Microsoft that are going to be specific to an Organization, then those users who already logged in via our existing social providers have to relink their accounts to the new Identity Provider. To them, they are already using either Google or Microsoft so is confusing and a little burdensome. 

### Details


I trust keycloak developer's and community's judgement on this, everything else has been solid. The only thing I could think of that may be the path of least resistance is to be able to indicate if an Identity Provider is 'shared'

- if an identity provider is specific to an organization, shared being false would mean it disappears as a provider option anywhere else. This is the current behavior.
- if an identity provider shared is true, then it can stay available for other Organizations or non-organization based login, and the 'hide on login page' can be used to control which option is shown for organization and non-organization based login.
issues.title: Allow Identity Providers to be shared between Organizations

issues.body:
### Description

Currently, Keycloak uses hardcoded cache names throughout the project, such as sessions, work, and others. While this works well in isolated setups, it introduces certain limitations in more complex environments, particularly when Keycloak shares an Infinispan cluster with other services.

### Problems Identified:

1.  **Name Collisions in Shared Infinispan Clusters:** When Infinispan is used as a centralized caching solution across multiple applications, the use of generic cache names like sessions and work can lead to unintended conflicts and is not considered a best practice. Allowing customization (e.g., through prefixes) would enable better namespace isolation and avoid potential collisions.

2. **Limitations in Test and Pre-production Environments:** In scenarios where multiple Keycloak instances (e.g., dev, test, pre-prod) are configured to use the same Infinispan server, identical hardcoded cache names prevent them from coexisting. This forces teams to provision separate Infinispan clusters for each environment, adding unnecessary operational overhead.


### Discussion

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions/38024

### Motivation and benefits

- Enables safer multi-tenant or multi-application Infinispan clusters.
- Simplifies CI/CD pipelines by allowing shared resources in non-production environments.
- Aligns with best practices for avoiding generic cache names in distributed caching systems.

### Details and solution

Introduce the ability to configure cache names via environment variables or configuration files, or at least allow setting a custom prefix for all Keycloak cache names. This change would improve flexibility and scalability, supporting advanced deployment scenarios without significant infrastructure duplication.
issues.title: Feature Request: Configurable Cache Names or Prefix Support for Infinispan Integration

issues.body:
This issue is about support for the delegation as mentioned in the token exchange specification. The most relevant specification sections:
- https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8693#name-delegation-vs-impersonation
- https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8693#name-act-actor-claim
- https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8693#name-may_act-authorized-actor-cl
- https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8693#name-delegation-token-exchange-e (Example. It is in the end of the specs, but maybe best to start with to grasp what the delegation is about)

## Notes and considerations

Some random notes here for now. Comments welcome on this issue about the possible use-cases and if the notes from here makes sense to cover your particular use-case.

- Delegation is IMO better and safer than "subject impersonation" (subject impersonation is the case when the token `sub` is required to be changed) due to this:
  - The delegation does not change the `sub` claim. So the exchanged token still has same user in the `sub` claim as the original `subject_token` had.
  - The great thing is, that exchanged token from the delegation contains both `sub` and `act` claims. Hence the exchanged token has all the informations like `This token has subject of user "normal-user", but the actor using this token is "admin-user"` . It gives some additional info to resource-server applications as they can differentiate between the case when the token is:
    - Normal token issued to the `sub` user where the actor is really the `sub` user (Normal use-case)
    - Delegated token with both `sub` and `act` claims where the application knows that actor is really the admin user.

- Do we need to support delegation just with `requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token` ? Or do we need to support also refresh tokens? Access tokens are easier and more safe IMO and can be nice if we can start just with supporting those (unless there are requirements for refresh tokens)

- Do we want to allow the delegation just if the `may_act` claim is present in the `subject_token` as shown in the example in the token exchange specification (link above)? It will be nice if we can start with requiring `may_act` claim IMO

- Question is, how is the `may_act` claim created in the subject token in the first place? Note that this is even before the token-exchange request itself (as it is relevant to issuing the `subject_token` during initial authentication). I can see some potential for "dynamic client scopes" (which are experimental feature at the time of this writing).

- I guess that in many cases, it could be great to show the consent screen to the user like `Grant admin user to act on your behalf` during initial authentication. It can be perhaps useful if this consent screen is shown even if client has `Consent Required` OFF 
 
### Example delegation scenario 

1) Initial authentication is done by user `user` . The initial OIDC request will contain something like `scope=may_act:admin` (would require dynamic client scopes)

- The consent screen is shown to the user `Grant user 'admin' to act on your behalf` (optional)

- The client scope `may_act` would contain some protocol mapper, which will add the `may_act` claim to the subject-token for user `admin`

2) User `admin` authenticates in the meantime to receive his own token (later being used as `actor_token`)

3) The token-exchange request is sent with `subject_token=subject-token-from-step-1&actor_token=admin-token-from-step-2`

4) Token exchange request would need to verify both `subject_token` and `actor_token` . Besides normal verifications of `actor_token` (session exists, user exists and is enabled etc), it should be verified that `actor_token` subject MUST be the same as `subject_token` subject from `may_act` claim. Verified tokens added as notes to `KeycloakSession` (ideal is if we don't need to persist `subject_token` and `actor_token` into clientSession)

5) Some protocol mapper, which will add `act` claim to the exchanged token as long as verified `subject_token` and `actor_token` are present in the KeycloakSession. In case of exchanging to refresh-tokens, some claim should be added to the isseued refreshToken, so that further refreshes of that refresh-token can add `act` claim as well.
issues.title: Support for token-exchange delegation

### Description

Epic created as a follow-up to https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/31546 to collect tasks related to Impersonation token exchange.

### Description

When an administrator invites a member to an organization via the "Organizations" section in the Keycloak Admin Console, and the invited user does not yet exist in Keycloak, an invitation email is sent with an expiration time. However, there is currently no way to track these pending invitations within Keycloak once they are sent. Since the user hasn’t been created yet, there’s no record tied to an existing user, and administrators lose visibility into which invitations remain unaccepted or have expired.

I propose adding a feature to the "Organizations" section of the Admin Console to display a list of pending invitations for each organization, including:

- Email Address: The email address of the invited user.
- Invitation Sent Date: The date and time when the invitation was sent.
- Expiration Status: Whether the invitation link is still valid.
- Acceptance Status: Whether the invitation has been accepted (e.g., "Pending" or "Accepted").

### Discussion

### Motivation

This would allow administrators to monitor outstanding invitations, resend them if needed, or clean up expired ones, improving the management of organization onboarding.

issues.body:
### Description

Admin REST API is a key part of Keycloak. Nearly every configuration interface (UI, CLI, Operator, …) uses it as its backend. As it evolved over the years of Keycloak’s existence, it needed to cover more and more areas with an increasing number of use cases and types of API clients. This explosive growth led to many design issues and inconsistencies making it difficult or sometimes even impossible for the API clients to use it for certain scenarios.

A new version of Admin API will aim to resolve the issues.

### Goals
* Blueprint for the new API
    * Includes designs and prototypes for proofing them.
        * Focused on the Keycloak Clients area as that will be the first to get implemented.
        * Designs and prototypes cover all use cases of the API. That includes:
            * The API itself
            * All first party clients: CLI, Java, JS/Admin Console, Operator, Terraform Provider
            * Docs
    * The result of the designs and prototypes is a document with final guidelines that can be used when implementing any part of the API.
* Implementation of the new API
    * Created as v2
        * Current Admin API (which will be marked as v1) will coexist with it it
    * Will be done incrementally.
        * Area by area, with each area also being implemented iteratively.
    * Won’t clash with v1, v1 and v2 can be used side by side so users can gradually migrate as new areas are implemented.
        * This applies both for the API itself and its clients too.
* Deprecation of the v1 API.

This is an umbrella issue for tracking the long-term effort for Admin API v2. The list of sub-issues will be updated over time.

* [x] #39222

### Motivation

The current API is suffering from many design issues. Fixing those issues requires redesigning the API from scratch as it is not viable to fix the existing API due to how extensive the changes need to be.

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions/37655 covers known issues with the current API.

issues.body:
### Description

Currently, Keycloak does not provide a way to grant a user read-only administrative access to all existing realms and automatically extend this access to any realms created in the future. The only global roles available are `admin` and `create-realm`, and realm-specific roles must be assigned manually for each realm. This limitation makes it difficult to manage organization-wide audit, reporting, or monitoring users who require consistent, read-only access across all realms.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

- **Centralized Audit and Monitoring**: Organizations often need to grant security, audit, or monitoring teams read-only access to all realms for compliance, troubleshooting, or reporting.
- **Operational Efficiency**: Manually assigning roles for each new realm is error-prone and does not scale in environments with frequent realm creation and deletion.
- **Consistency**: Ensures that read-only users always have up-to-date access, reducing risk of missed realms and inconsistent permissions.

### Details

 **Proposed Solution**
- Introduce a new global admin role (e.g., `global-read-only-admin`) in the master realm.
- This role would grant read-only access (equivalent to `view-*` roles) for all current and future realms, including the ability to view configuration, users, clients, and other realm resources without making modifications.
- The role should automatically apply to any realms created after assignment, without requiring manual updates.

**Alternatives Considered**
	•	Current workaround is to manually assign `view-*` roles for each realm client in the master realm and repeat this process for every new realm. This is not scalable and introduces operational overhead.

This feature would align with best practices for RBAC in large-scale, multi-tenant environments and is a common requirement in enterprise deployments.
issues.title: Global Read-Only Admin Role for All Realms (Including Future Realms)

issues.body:
### Description

The Workflows feature aims to empower Keycloak administrators to automate the management of realm resources. While administrators can manage the lifecycle of resources through the existing APIs, we lack a feature that automates the management of resources by executing actions on specific conditions, such as disabling users after a configured inactivity period. Instead, the administrator has to actively manage the realm resources - a task that can be tedious, time consuming, and error-prone.

Adding a feature that can automate certain user-related tasks, such as disabling, notifying or even removing users after a period of inactivity, is a huge step towards building an identity governance model for Keycloak. It also helps to reduce both the attack surface of the realm data and the cost that comes with keeping unused resources in the database.

The core of the new feature centers on automating the management of user resources through time-based policies. However, the design should accommodate the future expansion to include the management of other resources such as clients, brokers and organizations.

This is a follow-up of the transient users feature, giving administrators an option to not store user-related information permanently, but only for an adequate and configurable period of time.

### Discussion

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions/10370

### Motivation

Main motivation for this feature is to starting building an identity governance model for Keycloak, allowing admins to define policies for notifying, disabling, or even removing users after a configurable amount of time. Expanding on this idea, other resources could also be managed using these policies. 

For example, a client or identity broker that hasn't been used for authentication for a long time could be automatically disabled or removed, reducing the cost of storing and managing all these stale resources indefinitely and simplifying the server administration.

issues.body:
### Description

This feature proposes encrypting sensitive materials (e.g., private keys, secrets) managed by Keycloak’s `Imported*KeyProvider` and `Generated*KeyProvider` classes before persisting them to the database. Currently, these materials are stored in plaintext, exposing them to risks if the database is compromised. The encryption would leverage a configurable secret key (e.g., from a VaultProvider, KeyStore, environment variable, or file) to ensure confidentiality at rest.

References:
- https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak-community/blob/main/design/secure-credentials-store.md

### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

The motivation for this feature stems from several key factors:

1. **Security Best Practices:** Sensitive cryptographic materials should never be stored in plaintext. Encryption mitigates risks of unauthorized access to keys, which could lead to impersonation, data breaches, or token forgery.

2. **Compliance Requirements:** Regulations like GDPR mandate encryption of sensitive data. Keycloak’s current lack of encryption for KeyProvider materials creates compliance hurdles.

3. **Zero-Trust Posture:** Encrypting keys aligns with zero-trust principles, ensuring that even if the database is breached, attackers cannot misuse stored secrets without the encryption key.

4. **User Demand:** Many organizations using Keycloak in regulated industries explicitly require encryption for secrets at rest.

5. **I like that:** 😎

### Details

The proposed feature is designed to be implemented in a backward-compatible manner, ensuring that existing key provider implementations continue to function without modification, while also providing a clear migration path for administrators to enable encryption for existing key materials. Flexibility to support different encryption algorithms in the future is also incorporated.

1. **Encryption Design:**

  - A symmetric encryption algorithm (e.g., AES-GCM) is used to encrypt private keys and secret materials before storing them in the database.
  - A new boolean configuration property `encrypted` is introduced in the `COMPONENT_CONFIG` table to indicate whether the key material is encrypted.
    - Key materials stored in the `COMPONENT_CONFIG` table currently exist in various formats. A standard format, such as JWE (JSON Web Encryption) or PKCS#8, will be adopted for encrypted materials to ensure consistency and ease of decryption.
  - A new string configuration property `encryptionKeyAlias` is introduced in the `COMPONENT_CONFIG` table to store the alias of the encryption key.
    - The `VaultProvider` retrieves the encryption key, avoiding plaintext storage in the database. The alias stored in `COMPONENT_CONFIG` references the encryption key in the configured vault provider.

2. **Affected Components:**

  - **KeyProvider Implementations:** The following classes (and other relevant classes) will be modified to encrypt/decrypt secrets during persistence/retrieval:
    - `GeneratedAesKeyProvider`
    - `GeneratedEcdhKeyProvider`
    - `GeneratedEcdsaKeyProvider`
    - `GeneratedEddsaKeyProvider`
    - `GeneratedHmacKeyProvider`
    - `ImportedRsaKeyProvider`
  - **Database Schema:** No schema changes are required, but the `COMPONENT_CONFIG` table will store new properties for each key provider:
    - `encrypted`: boolean (default: `false`)
    - `encryptionKeyAlias`: string (used only if `encrypted` is `true`)

3. **Migration Strategy:**

  - **Migration steps:**
    1. The `encrypted` property is inferred as `false` for existing keys. If unset, the material is treated as unencrypted.
    2. When enabling encryption (setting `encrypted` to `true`), the administrator is required to provide the `encryptionKeyAlias` via a vault provider.
    3. Upon configuration, the key material is encrypted and stored in the database with the `encryptionKeyAlias`.

4. **Changing Already Encrypted Keys:**

  - To change the encryption key, the `encryptionKeyAlias` is updated to a new value. Existing materials are decrypted with the old key and re-encrypted with the new key. Both keys must be temporarily available in the vault provider.

5. **Algorithm Flexibility:**

  - Initial support for AES-GCM will be provided. The design accommodates future algorithms (e.g., ChaCha20). The chosen algorithm is stored in the key material (via JWE or PKCS#8), enabling backward-compatible additions.
issues.title: Encrypt KeyProvider's private key and secret materials

issues.body:
### Description

When Keycloak has OIDC IDP provider configured and sends the initial OIDC authentication request to the OIDC IDP, it uses `state` parameter.

From the Keycloak/RHBK 26, the length of the `state` parameter is longer than in previous versions, which causes issues in case of some identity providers, which don't support very long `state` parameters. This is due the fact that Keycloak now encodes also "client data" into the `state` parameter, which means that it is longer. Related issue where this was added is https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/24112 .

The long `state` parameter is the issue at least for Microsoft EntraID and for SingPass (a Singapore identity provider for access to government online services). For Microsoft EntraID, there is possibility to use POST method (Related issue https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/40042 . For the SingPass, POST method may not help as `state` has limited size even for `POST` method.

This issue is about adding the option like `Requires short state parameter` to the OIDC IDP (maybe also to the OAuth2 IDP, but not sure...). When this is enabled, there will not be an attempt to encode `client_data` into the `state` parameter, which is sent to the IDP.

Note there is the method `supportsLongStateParameter()` on the `IdentityProvider`, which currently always return true for all OAuth/OIDC providers. This issue means that providers, which has in the configuration `Requires short state parameter=true` will return false from `supportsLongStateParameter()` .

**NOTE:** Having option `Requires short state parameter` means that option could be disabled by default and needs to be explicitly enabled, which is the desired behaviour compatible with previous versions when migrating from Keycloak 26 or Keycloak 26.2.

**NOTE:** Related test is `KcOidcMultipleTabsBrokerTest` where new test case might be added for the scenario with the `Requires short state parameter`. The side-effect of not including `client_data` is that when OIDC IDP redirects back to the KEycloak with OIDC authentication response, but Keycloak has authenticationSession already expired (which could be due the longer time or due the fact that user already authenticated to Keycloak in different browser tab), the Keycloak does not have `client_data` and hence it will need to display the error page instead of being able to redirect back to the client. The error page might be for example the page like `You are already logged-in` in case that user was already logged in different browser tab. The similar test is in the `KcSamlMultipleTabsBrokerTest` as SAML never supports long state parameter (it is explicitly mentioned in the SAML specs that `RelayState` parameter has limited length).

**NOTE:** It might be possible to use cookie and encode "client data" into that cookie, however not 100% sure as cookie does not work in multiple browser tabs and also will need some expiration etc. So maybe we can consider cookie rather as a follow-up if needed.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

_No response_

### Details

### Description

At present, Keycloak offers built-in support only for Google reCAPTCHA to protect public forms (such as login, registration, and forgotten password). While reCAPTCHA is widely used, it introduces multiple concerns:

    Privacy: reCAPTCHA collects user data and is not privacy-friendly by design.

    Vendor lock-in: relying solely on a single proprietary CAPTCHA provider contradicts the open-source philosophy of Keycloak.

    Compliance: in some regions (such as the EU), organizations may face compliance issues with Google services.

There are some community-contributed hCaptcha plugins, but they suffer from several problems:

    They are often outdated and no longer actively maintained.

    They require manual modifications to Keycloak themes or templates.

    They are fragile with Keycloak updates and frequently break compatibility, leading to maintenance overhead.

Proposal:

Please consider implementing native support for hCaptcha alongside reCAPTCHA in the official Keycloak distribution. This should ideally be configurable in the Admin Console in the same way as reCAPTCHA, without requiring any manual theme edits.

Why hCaptcha?

    hCaptcha is an open and privacy-friendly alternative to reCAPTCHA.

    It is widely adopted and provides a compatible challenge-response system.

    It allows organizations to comply with stricter privacy regulations.

    It aligns with Keycloak’s mission as an open-source identity provider by giving administrators freedom of choice.

Benefits:

    Reduces dependence on Google services.

    Improves compliance options for organizations in regulated sectors.

    Avoids the risks associated with outdated community plugins.

    Offers a straightforward way to enhance security without compromising privacy.

Suggested Implementation:

    Provide hCaptcha as a built-in feature selectable via the existing CAPTCHA configuration UI.

    Allow specifying the hCaptcha site key and secret key through the Admin Console.

    Ensure the server-side verification and client-side widget are fully integrated, just like reCAPTCHA.

    Make the feature optional and fully backward-compatible.

hcaptcha repo can be found here:

https://github.com/hcaptcha
issues.title: Add native hCaptcha support as an alternative to reCAPTCHA

### Description

Why OpenTelemetry? Modern systems are increasingly **distributed, dynamic, and complex**. To understand, operate, and debug them effectively, teams need comprehensive observability across services, layers, and infrastructure.

**[OpenTelemetry (OTEL)](https://opentelemetry.io/)** is the emerging standard for collecting and exporting observability data — **logs, metrics, and traces** — in a vendor-neutral, consistent, and scalable way.

### Value Proposition

By adopting OTEL, we benefit from:

- **Unified instrumentation**: One consistent API and SDK for all signal types
- **Vendor-agnostic export**: Freedom to choose (and change) backends like Prometheus, Jaeger, Tempo, or commercial APMs
- **Correlated insights**: Combine logs, metrics, and traces for a complete picture of what happened and why

**OpenTelemetry brings logs, metrics, and traces signals together into one coherent ecosystem**, making observability easier to implement, scale, and evolve.

> Embracing OTEL across logs, metrics, and traces gives us full-spectrum visibility — essential for running reliable, maintainable systems.

#### 1. OpenTelemetry Logs 

As we already support OpenTelemetry Quarkus extension (see 3. OpenTelemetry Traces), providing OTel Logs is low-hanging fruit to integrate with Keycloak. 

Quarkus quide: [Using OpenTelemetry Logging](https://quarkus.io/guides/opentelemetry-logging)

> OpenTelemetry Logging is in _preview_ mode, so we need to make it preview even for Keycloak 

#### 2. OpenTelemetry Metrics 

Currently, Keycloak uses Micrometer for managing metrics with the pull mechanism as external monitoring system (like Prometheus) periodically scrapes the metrics from the `/metrics` endpoint. Dealing with OpenTelemetry and propagating metrics to OTel collector might be challenging within the current form.

However, Quarkus introduced a new extension for [Micrometer to OpenTelemetry bridge](https://quarkus.io/guides/telemetry-micrometer-to-opentelemetry). When we include the extension to Keycloak, without any major effort, we're able to push metrics (created by Micrometer) to the OTel collector.

Therefore, it might be the way we should go (it is even productized). You can find more information here: https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/41006

Quarkus quide: [Micrometer and OpenTelemetry extension](https://quarkus.io/guides/telemetry-micrometer-to-opentelemetry)

> Micrometer to OpenTelemetry bridge is in _preview_ mode, so we need to make it preview even for Keycloak 

#### 3. OpenTelemetry Traces 

We already support OpenTelemetry for Tracing. See https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/28581

### Goals

* Provide general options for telemetry settings
* Preview support for OpenTelemetry Logs
* Preview support for Micrometer to OpenTelemetry bridge for metrics 

### Non-Goals

* Deploy test environment with the full OpenTelemetry observability stack
* Benchmarking
issues.title: OpenTelemetry Support

issues.body:
### Description

(Thanks [@mabartos](https://github.com/mabartos) for your input!)

## Summary proposal
- Enterprises that already rely on Keycloak for Identity & Access Management increasingly need governed lifecycle controls - approvals, segregation-of-duties, and auditability - without adopting an external IGA suite.  
- The community proof-of-concept at **[tide-foundation/keycloak-IGA](https://github.com/tide-foundation/keycloak-IGA)** shows that with a small set of changes we can embed basic IGA into the Keycloak core.
- This epic proposes upstreaming a minimal, optional IGA feature-set (hidden behind a feature flag) to satisfy those use-cases while keeping vanilla Keycloak lean.

---

## Walkthrough / demo  

[![Native Keycloak IGA Walkthrough](http://img.youtube.com/vi/BrTBgFM7Lq0/0.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BrTBgFM7Lq0 "Native Keycloak IGA Walkthrough")

* [You can build and run the PoC yourself here: tide-foundation/keycloak-IGA](https://github.com/tide-foundation/keycloak-IGA)
---
## Problem Statement  
Keycloak today applies changes to users, roles, and clients immediately. That is ideal for agility, but it leaves no native mechanism for:

* draft / approval workflows before high-impact changes go live,  
* role-assignment governance and composite-role life-cycle control,  
* quorum-based delegations that let multiple realm-admins approve critical updates, and  
* auditability of “who approved what, when” within Keycloak itself.

Organizations therefore bolt on external IGA platforms or write bespoke tooling, adding complexity and latency.

---

## Proposed Solution (high-level)

| Work-stream | Goal |
|-------------|------|
| **1. IGA MVP** | Provide optional User, Realm, Client and Role providers that wrap existing JPA models with governance metadata and draft status. |
| **2. Drafting & Approval Workflow** | Any change that modifies effective access is stored in a pending state until approved. |
| **3. Quorum & Delegation Engine** | Realm-admins can be delegated; changes require a configurable percentage of current realm-admins (default 70 %). |
| **4. Admin UI & REST** | Add a small console plugin and REST endpoints for viewing pending drafts, approving / rejecting, and viewing audit history. |
| **5. Migration & Compatibility** | No schema changes unless the IGA profile is enabled; zero impact on existing deployments. |
| **6. Documentation & Operator Hooks** | Describe how to enable the IGA profile in container images and the Keycloak Operator. |

---

## Non-Goals  

* Full-blown segregation-of-duties (SoD) policy modelling  
* Ticketing-system integrations  
* External provisioning (SCIM, HR feeds)  
* Reporting UI beyond basic audit-log export  

---

## Benefits  

* **Security** – Removes god-mode power from a single admin.  
* **Compliance** – Reduces audit findings where four-eyes approval of entitlements is mandatory.  
* **Developer Experience** – Keeps governance in the same platform and API developers already use.  
* **Incremental Adoption** – IGA profile can be enabled per realm or cluster for a phased rollout.  
* **Community Alignment** – Builds on an existing OSS PoC, preventing ecosystem fragmentation.  

---

## References  

* [tide-foundation/keycloak-IGA](https://github.com/tide-foundation/keycloak-IGA) README (feature summary and SPI list)  
* Keycloak SPI developer guide  
* CNCF Security & Audit WG recommendations for least privilege and change control

### Discussion

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions/41350

### Issues

_No response_

### Motivation

_No response_
issues.title: Introduce foundational Identity Governance & Administration (IGA) capabilities into Keycloak

issues.body:
### Description

`SPIFFE and SPIRE provide strongly attested, cryptographic identities to workloads across a wide variety of platforms`

Workloads can leverage either X.509 SVID or JWT SVID when authenticating. In Keycloak clients can authenticate via mTLS, but using mTLS is a more complicated setup for SPIFFE/SPIRE and a simpler integration would be via JWT SVID.

Supporting SPIFFE/SPIRE can be broken down into the following milestones:

### Milestones

#### Milestone 1 - Support configuring a client to authenticate via JWT SVID

Ability to leverage SPIFFE JWT IDs to authenticate one or more clients within Keycloak.

Keycloak already supports [JSON Web Token (JWT) Profile
      for OAuth 2.0 Client Authentication and Authorization Grants ](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7523) that provides the basic capabilities required for this. However, there are a few issues that prevents this from working currently:

* Keycloak requires the `jti` claim, which is not issued by SPIFFE/SPIRE. This [claim is optional](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7523#section-3) in JSON Web Token (JWT) Profile
      for OAuth 2.0 Client Authentication and Authorization Grants
* Keycloak requires the token issuer to be identical to the client id. For JWT SVID the issuer will be SPIFFE/SPIRE and not the client
* Keycloak requires the subject to be the client id. A workaround would be to use something like `spiffe://example.org/myclient` for the client id, but we may want some form of mapping between the clients SPIFFE ID and the ID within Keycloak

#### Milestone 2 - Introduce a central trusted token issuer

In milestone 1 each individual client will need to be configured with the SPIFFE/SPIRE as the token issuer, and the relevant keys.

With a central trusted token issuer concept (think identity providers) the SPIFFE/SPIRE server can be configured once within a realm and a client can be linked to the token issuer instead of duplicating.

We can extend on the concept of identity providers for this purpose, and introduce identity providers that are not used for delegated authentication of users only, but also for delegated authentication of clients.

This can in the future also help with things like allowing mapping of the tokens issued by SPIFFE/SPIRE through protocol mappers.

#### Milestone 3 - Support dynamic client registration with SPIFFE/SPIRE

In the previous milestones the client has to be created first, but once we have the concept of a trust relationship with SPIFFE/SPIRE we can also allow clients to dynamically register themselves using their JWT SVID.
