issues.body:
### Description

Keycloak verifies WebAuthn attestation statements against certificates imported into the truststore and can restrict authenticators with a static AAGUID allow-list, but it has no access to the metadata the FIDO Alliance publishes for authenticator models. 
This enhancement adds a `webauthn-metadata` SPI with a FIDO Metadata Service (MDS) provider, uses the attestation root certificates from the metadata as trust anchors, and adds two policy options based on the metadata:  

a minimum **Authenticator certification** level and **Acceptable key protection types**.

### Value Proposition

Administrators can express requirements in terms the FIDO ecosystem already defines, such as "FIDO Certified Level 2 or higher" or "key protected by a secure element", instead of maintaining AAGUID lists by hand. Revoked or compromised authenticator models are rejected automatically. The metadata also supplies the attestation roots needed to verify AAGUIDs, which removes the need to import vendor root certificates into the truststore one by one, and provides display names for authenticator models missing from the built-in list.

### Goals

- `webauthn-metadata` SPI (`org.keycloak.webauthn.metadata`) with a `fido-mds` provider: remote MDS3 BLOB (`blob-url`) with signature and certificate chain verification against the MDS root (GlobalSign Root CA - R3 bundled, `root-certificate` overridable, optional CRL `revocation-check`), or a local BLOB file (`blob-file`, relative paths resolved against `conf/`) for environments without internet access. Background prefetch, refresh after the BLOB's `nextUpdate`, last good BLOB kept on failure with a retry backoff. Lookups by AAGUID and, for U2F, by attestation certificate key identifier.
- Attestation roots from the metadata merged with the truststore anchors in the attestation chain verification.
- Policy options on both WebAuthn policies: `authenticatorCertification` (`not specified`, `listed`, `FIDO_CERTIFIED`, `FIDO_CERTIFIED_L1` … `FIDO_CERTIFIED_L3plus`) and `acceptableKeyProtectionTypes` (`software`, `hardware`, `tee`, `secure_element`, `remote_handle`, `sync_fabric`). Both require an attestation format other than `none` and disable self attestation; `REVOKED` and the compromise statuses reject the model regardless of level.
- Credential display name falls back to the metadata description when the AAGUID is not in the built-in passkey metadata file.
- Admin console, documentation, unit and integration tests.

### Non-Goals

- A native, browser-free authentication API for mobile apps.
- Enforcing the metadata status at authentication time; the metadata is consulted at registration only.
- Replacing the built-in AAGUID display-name file with MDS data; MDS only complements it.
- Automatic activation. The provider stays inactive until a BLOB URL or file is configured.

### Discussion

Related: #46400

### Notes

- Additional `webauthn4j-metadata` library with the same version as the existing `webauthn4j-core`, needs to be added to the distribution. It pulls `jackson-datatype-jsr310`, which Quarkus already provides.
- The webauthn4j-metadata can download a file (blob.jwt) from the fido metadata service (MDS: https://fidoalliance.org/metadata/) or work with a fixed configured local file. The blob.jwt file contains the known devices with their AAGUIDs and a classification.
- Suggested testing approach: Chrome's virtual authenticator signs attestations with a fixed, public key and subject, so a self-signed certificate for that key works as MDS trust anchor in a generated test BLOB (`WebAuthnMetadataPolicyTest`, `FidoMdsServerConfig`). Unit tests cover the policy verifier, the store (indexing, backoff, stale serving) and the factory (file resolution, root certificate loading).
issues.title: WebAuthn authenticator metadata SPI with FIDO Metadata Service provider

issues.body:
### Description

This is a follow-up to #52188, which I opened. The fix in #53225 resolves the case where the other group has no permission or only a `view`/`manage` permission, but my scenario (each group delegated to a different admin with member scopes) is still blocked on 26.8.0 and 26.8.1, by design according to the new documentation. I'm opening this feature request to discuss restoring the FGAP v1 behavior for this use case.

With FGAP v2, delegated group administration breaks as soon as users belong to several groups delegated to different admins.

Setup:
- One delegated admin per group. Each group has its own Groups permission, granted only to its delegated admin, with scopes `["view", "view-members", "manage-membership", "manage-members"]` (`view-members` is required for the group's Members tab).
- A Users (all users) permission with `view` and `manage-group-membership` for the delegated admins.
- A user `jdoe` is a member of `groupe1` (delegated to `admin-groupe1`) and `groupe2` (delegated to `admin-groupe2`).

Result: `admin-groupe1` cannot open `jdoe` (403). Under UNANIMOUS, the permission on `groupe2` granted to `admin-groupe2` acts as a deny for `admin-groupe1` on the member scopes, and since #53225, denies on member scopes take precedence over user-level permissions. This is covered by `testViewUserMemberOfGroupDeniedByMemberScopeIsForbidden`.

The documented way to restore access, granting `view-members` on `groupe2` to `admin-groupe1`, would give `admin-groupe1` access to all members of `groupe2`, which defeats per-group delegation.

With FGAP v1, the same delegation model worked: the delegated admin could open the user, and only the groups they had access to were shown in the user's Groups tab.

### Value Proposition

Per-group delegation is one of the main use cases of fine-grained admin permissions, and in most organizations users belong to many groups (in our case, users commonly belong to dozens of LDAP groups, several of them delegated to different admins).

Today, with FGAP v2, there is no configuration where each delegated admin can both:
1. see and manage the members of their own group, and
2. open a user who also belongs to a group delegated to someone else.

This makes FGAP v2 unusable for multi-group delegation and blocks migration from FGAP v1, which supported this model. Restoring v1-equivalent behavior would allow organizations to adopt FGAP v2 without redesigning their delegation model.

### Goals

- A delegated admin with `view-members` (or `manage-members`) on at least one of a user's groups can view (or manage) that user, even if the user also belongs to groups delegated to other admins.
- The groups the delegated admin has no access to are filtered out of the user's group memberships, as in FGAP v1.
- An **explicit** deny (a negative policy on a group's member scopes) still protects the members of that group, as covered by `testViewUserDeniedOnlyForProtectedGroupMembers`.

### Non-Goals

- Granting the delegated admin any access to groups, or members of groups, they have no permission on.
- Changing the behavior of explicit negative policies on member scopes.
- Changing how FGAP v2 handles federated users or `LDAP_ONLY` memberships (tracked separately in #54403).

### Discussion

_No response_

### Notes

Possible approach (not a definitive design): distinguish an **implicit** deny (a permission that grants a scope to other admins, and therefore denies everyone else under UNANIMOUS) from an **explicit** deny (a negative policy). For member scopes:

- If the admin is granted the member scope on at least one of the user's groups, implicit denies coming from the user's other groups should not block access to the user; those groups are simply filtered out of the user's memberships.
- Explicit denies keep their current precedence and still protect the group's members.

This would restore FGAP v1 behavior for multi-group delegation while keeping the "protected group" use case introduced by #53225.

Related: #52188, #53225, #54403
issues.title: FGAP v2: allow delegated admins to access users who also belong to groups delegated to other admins (parity with v1)

### Description

When you remove a users passkey in Keycloak the user might still have the passkey in the used passkey authenticator. From the user perspective it is all done right when authenticating with a apparently valid passkey, but the server may reject if the passkey is unknown on it's side.

The WebAuthn Signal API can be used to tell a users authenticator to remove stale passkeys. The W3C explainer for this API can be found here: https://github.com/w3c/webauthn/blob/main/explainers/signal-api.md

### Value Proposition

A better user experience and more trust into passwordless authentication methods.

### Goals

Implement the respective methods from WebAuthn Signal API to tell a users authenticator to remove stale passkeys.

### Non-Goals

Browsers or setups that do not support the WebAuthn Signal API.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Notes

_No response_
issues.title: Leverage WebAuthn Signal API to remove stale passkeys on user-side

### Description

Introduce native support for configurable registration links within each Keycloak realm.

Realm administrators should be able to create multiple registration links, each associated with one or more existing groups. Users who register through these links should automatically be assigned to the configured groups upon successful registration.

Each registration link should have a unique identifier and be manageable through the Keycloak Admin Console and Admin REST API.

Optionally, administrators should be able to configure expiration dates, usage limits, and enable or disable individual links.

### Value Proposition

Currently, automatically assigning users to specific groups based on the registration link requires custom SPIs, registration flow extensions, or external integrations.

This feature would simplify user onboarding by providing a native, secure, and standardized mechanism for group-based registration.

It would be particularly valuable for multi-tenant applications, team onboarding, organizational invitations, and self-service registration workflows.

### Goals

Allow administrators to create multiple registration links per realm.

Associate each registration link with one or more existing groups.

Automatically assign registered users to the configured groups.

Manage registration links through the Admin Console and Admin REST API.

Support optional link expiration, usage limits, and revocation.

Ensure registration links cannot be manipulated to gain unauthorized group membership.

Preserve compatibility with existing registration flows, required actions, and realm security policies.

### Non-Goals

Replacing the existing Keycloak registration flow.

Creating new groups automatically through registration links.

Allowing users to select or modify their assigned groups during registration.

Supporting cross-realm registration or group assignments.

Implementing a complete invitation management system with email delivery.

Automatically changing group memberships for existing users.

Bypassing existing authentication, verification, or registration security requirements.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Notes

_No response_
issues.title: Realm-Specific Registration Links with Automatic Group Assignment

issues.body:
### Description

Add a new OIDC protocol mapper, `Child Group Membership`, that adds a `groups`
(or any configured claim name) to tokens containing only the names of the
groups that are children (direct or indirect) of a configured parent group.
Direct membership in the parent group itself is intentionally excluded --
only descendants count.


### Value Proposition

The built-in `Group Membership` mapper (`oidc-group-membership-mapper`) always
maps *all* of a user's groups. There is no built-in way to scope a `groups`
claim to a subtree of the group hierarchy (e.g. only expose groups under
`/engineering` to a client, without leaking unrelated groups like
`/marketing` or internal admin groups). Teams that model org units,
tenants, or feature entitlements as group subtrees currently have to build
and maintain a custom SPI implementation to get this behavior.


### Goals

- A new protocol mapper, selectable per client scope/client, with:
  - A "Parent group path" config field (e.g. `/engineering`).
  - A "Multivalued" toggle, consistent with other claim mappers.
  - Standard token-claim-name / include-in-token config shared with other
    OIDC mappers via `OIDCAttributeMapperHelper`.
- Supports both direct and transitive (indirect) child groups.
- Works for access token, ID token, userinfo, and introspection, matching
  the capabilities of `GroupMembershipMapper`.


### Non-Goals

- Changing the behavior of the existing `Group Membership` mapper.
- Supporting multiple parent group paths in a single mapper instance (can be
  achieved today by adding multiple mapper instances with different token
  claim names).

### Discussion

_No response_

### Notes

A working implementation already exists and will be submitted as a PR
referencing this issue:

`org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.mappers.ChildGroupMembershipMapper`, 


registered alongside the other mappers in
`services/src/main/resources/META-INF/services/org.keycloak.protocol.ProtocolMapper`,

with an integration test in
`tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/ChildGroupMembershipMapperTest.java`.
issues.title: Add OIDC protocol mapper for child-only group membership

### Description

Add an **add-skill** skill to the public **keycloak/keycloak** repository at **skills/add-skill/**. It should help contributors turn a task description or repeated workflow into a reusable AI skill following the Agent Skills format and repository conventions.

The existing [add-skill implementation in Keycloak AI Skills](https://github.com/lhanusov/keycloak-ai-skills/tree/main/skills/add-skill) can serve as a starting point.

### Value Proposition

Make skill authoring available directly in the Keycloak repository, helping contributors capture repeatable workflows with consistent instructions, clear outcomes, and validation.

### Goals

- Provide the skill at **skills/add-skill/SKILL.md**, with supporting resources where needed.
- Guide contributors through defining scope, inputs, expected results, and overlap with existing skills.
- Create new skills under the repository’s **skills/** folder by default.
- Keep shared instructions independent of a specific AI client.
- Validate naming, metadata, local references, and template completeness.
- Document how to invoke the skill.

### Non-Goals

- Automatically publishing or globally installing generated skills.
- Changing Keycloak runtime behavior.
- Replacing human review of generated instructions.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Notes

Adapt the existing implementation to the public Keycloak repository’s structure and contribution conventions.

Example invocation:

Use add-skill to create a skill for migrating a legacy Keycloak test to the new test framework.

The result should include the generated skill files under **skills/**, validation results, and invocation guidance.
issues.title: Add an add-skill AI skill for creating reusable contributor workflows
